The expected impact is faster cross-border onboarding, stronger legal-entity verification, reduced administrative burden and more secure business-to-government or business-to-business digital transactions. The wider EBSI framework also defines legal entity credential registry standards for publishing legal-entity verifiable credentials in an open and interoperable manner.

cases.context: London Borough of Harrow; Local Government; Fuel and energy; United Kingdom
cases.implementation: GovLaunch reported a potential annual bill reduction of up to 45% if implemented, while NewFrame reports that the three-kilowatt solar-glass array could deliver up to 68% of individual household energy bills throughout the year.

cases.source_description: Housing decarbonisation is particularly difficult in social housing because retrofit measures must reduce emissions and energy costs while remaining practical, affordable and acceptable for residents. In Harrow, Project-A.I.R explored a solar-glass structure concept intended to support household energy transition and reduce fuel poverty. The concept centres on a standalone transparent garden structure or pergola-canopy in which photovoltaic glass serves both as construction material and power-generating surface. The implementation brings together retrofit analysis, solar PV glass, a three-kilowatt peak array and the wider transition from fabric-first improvements to electric-powered homes. Public descriptions frame the initiative as AI-guided because the concept was identified and assessed through an approach designed to target efficient decarbonisation measures in housing. At a conceptual level, the solution combines household retrofit intelligence, semi-transparent solar generation, structural design and social-housing energy planning. The expected impact is reduced household energy bills, lower carbon emissions and a visible demonstration of renewable technology integrated into domestic space. GovLaunch reported a potential annual bill reduction of up to 45% if implemented, while NewFrame reports that the three-kilowatt solar-glass array could deliver up to 68% of individual household energy bills throughout the year. The project was presented publicly at Grand Designs Live in 2023.

cases.source_description: Judicial authorities often need to understand foreign-language documents quickly, but legal translation is sensitive, time-critical and unsuitable for generic public translation platforms when quality, confidentiality and data protection are required. In the German justice context, the project responds to the recurring need for rapid work translations across many languages, where in-house expertise may not be available and manual translation can be too slow or costly for initial case assessment. The objective is to help justice staff search and understand foreign-language material more effectively, while preserving control over legal data. The implementation uses neural machine translation trained on translated texts relevant to the judicial environment. At a conceptual level, foreign-language documents are processed through a secure translation system that produces immediate work translations, enabling users to obtain an overview, search documents more precisely and decide whether certified or expert translation is needed. A further development goal is translation memory: texts already processed as input or output are recognised and reused, improving consistency and efficiency over time. In regular operation, the system is intended to shift towards a central translation platform. The expected impact is faster access to multilingual legal material, lower thresholds for preliminary translations, reduced dependence on external platforms and better support for time-critical judicial workflows. Because legal meaning is context-dependent, the service remains a support tool rather than a substitute for authoritative legal translation.

cases.source_description: Derogations and transitional provisions are essential in legislation, but they can make legal obligations difficult to understand because they modify when, where or under what conditions a rule applies. This LEOS case study explores how classification and legal-text analysis can help identify derogations, connect them to the obligations they modify, and extract temporal or conditional parameters. The operational problem is that drafters and users may struggle to trace the relationship between a general rule and exceptions that appear elsewhere in a legal act or in related legislation. The implementation uses AI classification, legal annotation and structured analysis of normative text. At a conceptual level, the system detects clauses that create derogations or transitional regimes, identifies the initial obligations affected, and extracts information such as dates, durations, conditions and applicability criteria. These outputs can then support drafting review, legal navigation and clearer presentation of exceptions. The expected impact is improved legal clarity, fewer interpretative errors, better traceability of temporal rules and stronger support for digital legal services. For policy and drafting teams, the value is not automatic legal interpretation but earlier visibility of how exceptions interact with obligations. The use case was included in the European Commission’s LEOS smart-functionality study alongside pilots on corrigenda, transposition and digital readiness.

cases.source_description: Digital-ready legislation is increasingly important because laws and policies must be implementable through digital-by-default public services, data exchange and automated administrative processes. This LEOS case study investigates how smart drafting support could assess whether a legal act enables smooth digital implementation. The operational problem is that digital readiness is often assessed late or inconsistently, even though legislative wording can determine whether services can be automated, data can be reused and citizens can interact digitally with administrations. The proof of concept has three linked goals: calculate a digital-readiness index for a document, assess how normative citations and definitions propagate through the legal system, and develop a predictive model that estimates the index of new text fragments during drafting. The implementation uses legal-text analysis, citation analysis, modelling of definitions and predictive scoring. At a conceptual level, the system examines how a draft refers to other norms, how definitions affect implementation, and whether textual features support or hinder digital administration. The expected impact is earlier identification of provisions that may block digital-by-default services, better alignment between legal drafting and digital policy implementation, and more actionable feedback for drafters. The European Commission’s later LEOS work frames these cases as part of a broader move towards AI-based microservices that assist lawyers and policy developers while preserving human legal control.

cases.source_description: Access to justice can be hindered when citizens and organisations must physically attend court offices or navigate several separate portals to find information, forms and register services. JustizOnline was created as Austria’s digital gateway to the judiciary, bringing together online information, procedural services and access to registers in a single service environment. The operational objective is to reduce unnecessary court visits and help users find relevant functions more quickly, whether they need information on proceedings, court services, forms, the Companies Register, the Land Register or judicial announcements. The implementation includes the chatbot “Justitia”, which guides users to the relevant information and can answer simple justice-related questions. At a conceptual level, the platform combines digital self-service, secure authentication, linked e-government interfaces, register access and conversational navigation. Integration with other Austrian e-government portals reduces duplication by allowing representation and authorisation information to be managed consistently across connected services. The expected impact is easier access to justice, faster completion of routine interactions, fewer administrative barriers and more efficient communication between the judiciary and the public. JustizOnline is important because it treats digital justice as a service ecosystem rather than a single online form, supporting both information needs and transactional access to judicial services.

cases.source_description: Mountain water management depends on understanding how glacier melt contributes to downstream reservoirs, especially as climate change alters snow, ice and seasonal runoff dynamics. In Trentino, the Public AI Challenge applied artificial intelligence to the Careser Glacier in the Dolomites to reconstruct and forecast water flows towards reservoirs located downhill. The operational problem is that environmental monitoring datasets can contain gaps, missing measurements or discontinuities, making it harder for public authorities to understand hydrological conditions and anticipate changes in water availability. The implementation used dense neural-network techniques to estimate and reconstruct missing flow-rate data by learning relationships between available observations and expected water-flow patterns. At a conceptual level, the model supports prediction-measurement comparison: where sensor or historical data are incomplete, the neural network can infer plausible values and help reconstruct the hydrological series needed for environmental assessment. This creates a decision-support layer for monitoring glacier-fed systems, reservoir inflows and broader environmental status. The expected impact is improved continuity of hydrological monitoring, better evidence for water-resource planning and stronger public-sector capacity to use existing environmental datasets. The case is also relevant because it shows how an open-innovation challenge can introduce AI methods into provincial administration without requiring a full internal AI development team. Trentino Innovation describes the Public AI Challenge as a mechanism through which students develop predictive models and intelligent systems for public-administration needs.

cases.implementation: The Trentino / Garda-area AI for Water use case involved NIRIS and AI Challenge participants working on data from public water-treatment infrastructure to forecast incoming water variations using historical plant data and meteorological information. cases.source_description: Wastewater-treatment and water-infrastructure operators need to manage variable inflows while controlling energy consumption, maintenance risks and service continuity. The Trentino / Garda-area AI for Water use case involved NIRIS and AI Challenge participants working on data from public water-treatment infrastructure to forecast incoming water variations using historical plant data and meteorological information. The operational problem is that treatment plants consume significant energy, and rainfall-driven changes in inflow can create operational peaks that are expensive or inefficient if not anticipated. The implementation used historical purifier data, weather data from the Stenico area and machine-learning methods to identify correlations between meteorological conditions, anthropic impact and plant behaviour. At a conceptual level, the system learns from past inflow, weather and operational patterns to forecast future water loads, enabling plant managers to prepare equipment and optimise energy use. The expected impact is lower energy consumption, better remote management, improved predictive maintenance and more resilient operation of depuration infrastructure. The use case is notable because it applies AI to a highly practical utility-management problem, where small percentage savings can matter because water-treatment systems operate continuously and at high energy intensity across many plants.

cases.task: Fondo Caproni Project (AI for Culture)
cases.context: Provincia Autonoma di Trento; Regional Government; Cultural services.; Italy
cases.implementation: The implementation explored the use of artificial intelligence to automate parts of the catalogue-building process, with particular emphasis on image-quality assessment and primary thematic classification. Provincial material also confirms that the wider Caproni archive is being digitalised using PNRR funding, making the AI challenge part of a larger cultural-heritage digitisation trajectory.

cases.source_description: Large cultural collections can become difficult to preserve and make accessible when the volume of material exceeds the capacity of manual cataloguing teams. The Caproni Collection contains approximately 200,000 historic photographs and aviation-related assets, including valuable images, memorabilia and documentation linked to Italian aeronautical history. The administrative challenge is to count, catalogue, classify, preserve, assess image quality and prepare selected materials for public exposure without imposing unsustainable labour requirements on cultural staff. The implementation explored the use of artificial intelligence to automate parts of the catalogue-building process, with particular emphasis on image-quality assessment and primary thematic classification. At a conceptual level, computer-vision models can identify damaged, blurred or low-quality photographs, group images into broad themes, support metadata generation and prioritise items requiring human review or conservation attention. This does not remove curatorial responsibility, but it can shift expert effort towards validation, interpretation and public presentation. The expected impact is faster digitisation, improved quality control, better searchability and broader public access to the Caproni heritage. Provincial material also confirms that the wider Caproni archive is being digitalised using PNRR funding, making the AI challenge part of a larger cultural-heritage digitisation trajectory. The case demonstrates how AI can support public cultural institutions when archive scale makes purely manual processes impractical.

cases.problem: Traditional investigative tools struggle to cope with this complexity, leading to lengthy investigations and fragmented insights.
cases.task: I-CAN Police Crime Predictive System against Ndrangheta Network Crime
cases.context: Italian Department of Public Security; Central-Government; Public order and safety n.e.c.; Italy
cases.implementation: I-CAN is operational as an INTERPOL cooperation framework, with tools progressively deployed to support investigations.
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Investigating organised and transnational criminal networks such as the ’Ndrangheta requires law enforcement agencies to analyse vast volumes of heterogeneous data, including communications, financial records, multimedia material and relational information. Traditional investigative tools struggle to cope with this complexity, leading to lengthy investigations and fragmented insights. INTERPOL launched the I-CAN initiative to strengthen the analytical capacity of police forces involved in combating Italian mafia-type organisations, supporting national and cross-border investigations. Stakeholders include INTERPOL, national police forces, judicial authorities and specialised organised crime units. The objective is to accelerate investigations, improve detection of hidden criminal relationships and enhance international cooperation. The system builds on technologies developed in EU-funded research projects such as ROXANNE, integrating network analysis, multilingual text and speech processing, and video analysis into a single interoperable platform. Data from multiple investigative sources are correlated to generate visual network graphs, behavioural patterns and relationship mappings, while remaining compatible with existing law enforcement databases and legal safeguards. I-CAN is operational as an INTERPOL cooperation framework, with tools progressively deployed to support investigations. Reported impacts include faster case analysis, improved situational awareness, reduced investigative workload per case and stronger cross-border intelligence sharing, contributing to more effective disruption of organised crime networks.

The expected impact is improved city management, faster operational coordination, better regulation of water and land mobility, and more informed decisions during high-pressure events. The case is significant because it combines heritage-city governance with smart-city operations in a territory where urban management has both everyday and exceptional-risk dimensions.

cases.source_description: Schools and higher-education institutions face a pedagogical challenge when generative AI can produce coherent written answers, summaries and draft texts in response to ordinary prompts. This use case concerns the educational use of ChatGPT not as an autonomous teaching system, but as a tool for critical collaboration between students, teachers and AI-generated text. The operational issue is that students may use the system to produce assignments mechanically, while educators can instead redesign activities so that learners interrogate, verify, contextualise and improve AI outputs. The implementation is therefore mainly pedagogical: ChatGPT can be used to generate examples, draft outlines, propose questions, create exercises, provide writing models, support translation, or produce material that students then analyse against sources and disciplinary knowledge. At a conceptual level, the tool offers syntactically coherent and semantically connected responses, but it does not independently establish a situated, critical or interpretative perspective. The expected impact is a shift from banning AI to teaching students how to question it, evaluate its limitations and use it to accelerate constructive thinking. The case is particularly relevant in arts and humanities education, where human contextualisation, semiotic reading and critical interpretation remain central to the learning process.

More advanced analytical objectives include identifying patterns in awards and forecasting likely bidders or awardees under certain tender characteristics. The expected impact is better procurement transparency, more accurate public spending analysis, improved searchability of tenders and stronger evidence for policy, audit and market-intelligence work. The Finnish Tax Administration use case concerns the controlled use of artificial intelligence in taxation, within the legal framework governing tax assessment and administrative procedure. cases.context: Basque Country; Regional Government; Law courts; Spain
cases.implementation: The implementation uses neural-network-based speech-to-text technology capable of transcribing Spanish, Basque and bilingual Spanish-Basque audio or video content.

cases.source_description: Court proceedings generate large volumes of spoken material that may later need to be searched, quoted, reviewed or used in higher-instance appeals. In the Basque Country, Transkit was developed to reduce the burden of manually reviewing court-session videos and preparing transcripts. The operational problem is that legal staff may need to locate exactly where a phrase was said, who said it, or which named entities were mentioned, but manual video review is slow and does not create searchable text. The implementation uses neural-network-based speech-to-text technology capable of transcribing Spanish, Basque and bilingual Spanish-Basque audio or video content. At a conceptual level, the system converts recorded proceedings into timestamped text, links speech with searchable terms and allows staff to focus on correction, validation and completion rather than full manual transcription. The expected impact is faster judicial administration, improved productivity for clerks and court staff, easier review of appeal material, better searchability of proceedings and more efficient preparation of judgments or records. The tool does not replace official legal validation of transcripts; it provides a draft and search layer that supports human professionals in managing recorded procedural content more efficiently.

cases.source_description: Small islands face distinctive energy challenges because they often rely on isolated grids, imported fuels and limited flexibility, while renewable generation requires coordination between producers, consumers and local distributors. BloRin was developed for Sicilian islands such as Favignana and Lampedusa to test whether blockchain-based systems could support decentralised renewable-energy communities and transparent energy-service delivery. The objective is to manage exchanges between prosumers, aggregate distributed resources, support balancing services and coordinate energy flows without relying on opaque or intermediary-heavy processes. The implementation uses a blockchain-like platform for secure data transfer between users, developed with the University of Palermo and industrial partners including Exalto Energy & Innovation and Regalgrid. Tests are linked to Mediterranean island settings and the University of Palermo campus. At a conceptual level, the system records energy production, consumption, exchange and service-delivery information in a tamper-resistant environment, helping coordinate microgrid operations and interactions with electricity distributors. It can also support electric-vehicle charging infrastructure in vehicle-to-grid mode. The expected impact is greater transparency in renewable-energy management, stronger participation by local prosumers, better integration of distributed generation and a replicable model for sustainable small-island energy communities. Public sources continue to describe BloRin as a project being developed and tested, rather than a mature commercial utility platform.

cases.problem: Urban enforcement teams in busy nightlife and tourist areas must respond to nuisance quickly, but reports may arrive too late or lack precise location information.
cases.task: The Hague uses AI to reduce laughing gas nuisance
cases.context: Municipality of The Hague; Local Government; Police Services; Netherlands

cases.source_description: Urban enforcement teams in busy nightlife and tourist areas must respond to nuisance quickly, but reports may arrive too late or lack precise location information. In Scheveningen, The Hague tested whether smart cameras could help detect nitrous oxide, or laughing gas, abuse around the boulevard, where nuisance was linked to parking problems, traffic violations, noise and other undesirable behaviour. The objective was to give municipal enforcement staff timely information while avoiding unnecessary collection of identifiable footage. The implementation used AI-enabled cameras from Avutec trained to recognise nitrous oxide balloons and related paraphernalia, with Monotch’s TLEX platform forwarding detection data to the enforcement organisation. At a conceptual level, the system combines video analytics, object recognition, privacy-preserving event reporting and real-time notification workflows. Smart Cities World reports that no footage was sent because of privacy considerations; only detection data were forwarded. The pilot assessed algorithm functionality, camera accuracy, notification speed and privacy protection during a test day on the Scheveningen boulevard. The expected impact is quicker enforcement response, better targeting of patrols and reduced nuisance linked to laughing gas use, without creating a general-purpose surveillance stream. The test confirmed the algorithm’s functionality and gave a “green light” for refinement, but public sources describe it as a trial rather than full deployment.

cases.context: Brønnøysund Register Centre under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries; Central-Government; General economic, commercial and labour affair; Norway

cases.source_description: The economic shock of the COVID-19 pandemic required governments to deliver financial support quickly while still preventing fraud, error and misuse of public funds. Norway’s digital compensation scheme was created to help businesses withstand pandemic-related revenue losses through a highly automated application, verification and payment process. The operational objective was to provide rapid liquidity to eligible firms without creating a slow, manually administered grant system. Applications were approved by an auditor and then automatically processed through checks against multiple official sources and registers. At a conceptual level, the system combined digital application intake, pre-disbursement validation, register-based verification, automated decision support, transparency mechanisms and rapid payment workflows. Information about grants was published every hour, applicants could receive a reply within minutes, and payments were made within 72 hours. This design reduced the need for extensive post-payment verification because key checks were performed before disbursement, lowering both administrative burden and misconduct risk. The expected impact was fast crisis support, protection of business continuity, transparent use of public money and reusable capacity for future emergency schemes. The Norwegian case is a strong example of digital-era public administration: automation was used not merely for efficiency, but to combine speed, control, auditability and public transparency during an exceptional economic crisis.

At a conceptual level, the system analyses patterns in previous rehabilitation cases and translates them into recommendations or decision support for case managers, with performance measured through improved self-sufficiency and reduced reliance on home help. The expected impact is more consistent rehabilitation planning, better use of assistive aids, earlier fall-prevention attention and improved targeting of training resources. A proof-of-concept was conducted in 2018–2019, while the AIR signature project ran from 2020 to 2022 and delivered a prototype by the end of the project period.

Greater Manchester’s Violence Reduction Unit worked with Greater Manchester Magistrates’ Association and Round Midnight to deliver Virtual_Decisions, a prevention programme using virtual reality as part of a wider educational curriculum. cases.source_description: The Municipal Police of Prague operate an automated speed enforcement system to improve road safety and ensure compliance with traffic regulations. The system comprises over 60 devices across the city, including more than 40 section-control installations that calculate average speed between two points using induction loops embedded in the road surface, and around 20 radar-based cameras measuring instantaneous speed. Captured data include vehicle images and licence plate numbers, with automatic number plate recognition applied in designated subsystems. The technology processes speed measurements and generates violation records, producing approximately 300,000 fines annually. While detection and data processing are automated, all sanction decisions are reviewed by a human officer before issuance, ensuring procedural oversight. The system enhances enforcement coverage, increases consistency in speed control and supports deterrence of traffic offences. By combining automated measurement with human validation, Prague strengthens road safety management while maintaining administrative accountability.

cases.source_description: To ensure compliance with legal requirements for presidential candidacy, Czech authorities apply statistical verification to nomination signatures submitted by candidates. Candidates may qualify either through parliamentary support or by collecting 50,000 voter signatures. In the latter case, the Ministry of Interior conducts a statistical quality control process to verify that signatories are eligible voters. An algorithm randomly selects two batches of 8,500 signatures for detailed validation against population registers. Error rates identified in the samples are extrapolated to estimate the overall validity of submitted signatures. The process resembles statistical quality control methods used in auditing, enabling efficient review of large datasets without checking every entry individually. While the approach accelerates verification and standardises assessment, it has generated debate regarding sampling design and accuracy. In the 2013 election cycle, two candidates were excluded following application of this procedure. The system aims to balance administrative feasibility with electoral integrity safeguards.

cases.context: National Institute for Social Security (INPS); Central-Government; Social protection n.e.c.; Italy

cases.source_description: Labour platforms and gig workers often operate outside traditional social security frameworks, creating gaps in insurance coverage and administrative complexity for short-term or task-based work. In Italy, a concept known as the “Welfare Ticket” was developed to address these challenges by enabling temporary, portable social security coverage for gig economy workers. Stakeholders included employers, platform workers, and social security institutions, with the objective of simplifying compliance while ensuring that workers remained insured during the execution of specific tasks. The proposed solution centred on a shared digital register where employers could issue a time-bound social security ticket linked to a specific job. The platform design relied on distributed ledger technology to record the issuance, validity period, and redemption of welfare tickets in an immutable and auditable manner. Each transaction would be visible to authorised parties, reducing disputes and administrative reconciliation. Although the concept was developed through an enterprise design thinking process and documented by INPS, it did not progress to operational deployment. Nevertheless, the initiative provided a structured blueprint for how decentralised registers could support more flexible labour markets, influencing later discussions on portable benefits and digital welfare infrastructure.

cases.source_description: As feed-in tariffs are phased out, photovoltaic system operators face declining revenues, while consumers seek affordable green electricity. Traditional energy markets offer limited support for local energy exchange and self-consumption. The BloGPV project addresses this challenge by enabling local trading of solar electricity among neighbours through a virtual storage concept. Stakeholders include PV system operators, electricity consumers, and local energy communities. The objective is to maintain the economic viability of solar installations and strengthen local renewable energy use. The solution creates a distributed virtual storage network that connects producers and consumers, allowing surplus electricity to be traded locally. Automated transaction mechanisms record energy exchanges and settlements within the network, ensuring transparency and reliability. By coordinating production and consumption, the system reduces reliance on centralised grids and supports local balancing. The impact includes improved returns for solar producers, more attractive green electricity for consumers, and increased local self-sufficiency. BloGPV contributes to decentralised energy systems and offers a replicable model for community-based renewable energy trading.

cases.context: Kombiverkehr German Society for Combined Freight Transport mbH & Co. KG; Consortium; Transport; Germany
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Combined transport terminals must assign loading units to wagon sets efficiently, yet placement decisions often need to be made before complete information on incoming shipments is available. This creates operational uncertainty and can reduce utilisation of rail capacity. The KiBa project addresses this assignment problem by developing IT-based optimisation methods that generate rapid and efficient loading proposals under dynamic conditions. Discrete mathematical optimisation models are combined with machine learning techniques to calculate optimal placement of loading units on available wagons, considering route, weight and temporal constraints. The system processes partial and evolving data, updating recommendations as new information becomes available. By integrating predictive algorithms into terminal management systems, the solution supports near real-time decision-making. The approach improves wagon utilisation, reduces empty capacity and enhances planning reliability in combined transport operations. It contributes to more efficient rail logistics, lower operational costs and increased competitiveness of intermodal freight transport.

cases.source_description: Urban authorities require detailed and up-to-date traffic data to manage complex shared spaces safely, particularly in dense city centres where interactions between vehicles, cyclists and pedestrians are frequent. The LiDARshared project equips public buses with high-performance LiDAR sensors to collect comprehensive three-dimensional traffic data during regular operations. In cooperation with stakeholders in Kiel, sensor-equipped buses capture detailed information on traffic flows, road geometry and movement patterns along main arteries and busy intersections. The collected data are processed using advanced spatial analytics to identify congestion points, risk zones and behavioural patterns. Results can inform adjustments to traffic light phases, speed limits, one-way regulations and targeted safety interventions for vulnerable road users. By leveraging existing public transport fleets as mobile sensing platforms, the project enables cost-efficient, large-scale data acquisition. The initiative supports smarter traffic management, enhances road safety and provides a scalable data foundation for future autonomous mobility applications.

cases.context: Erfurt University of Applied Sciences, Faculty of Economics, Logistics, Transport; Academic-Research; Transport; Germany
cases.implementation: Based on reference scenarios and interface analyses, a forecasting model was developed to predict time- and location-specific occupancy rates using available traffic and infrastructure data.

cases.source_description: Overcrowding at truck rest areas along heavily used federal highways leads to safety risks, inefficient parking searches and uneven utilisation of available capacity. Despite infrastructure investments, demand peaks in the evening and at night continue to strain facilities. The PAHA project examined how predictive and networked control systems could harmonise occupancy across rest areas. Based on reference scenarios and interface analyses, a forecasting model was developed to predict time- and location-specific occupancy rates using available traffic and infrastructure data. Model-predictive control approaches generate recommendations for optimal rest areas tailored to individual vehicles, incorporating static and dynamic variables such as current occupancy and travel time. The concept integrates Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication to transmit guidance directly to drivers. Requirements for upgrading existing large-scale occupancy detection systems were identified to enable integration of forecasting and control functions. The approach promises improved utilisation of parking capacity, reduced congestion and enhanced safety and efficiency in long-distance freight transport.

The Shuttles &Co project established a digital test field in Berlin to trial automated fleet vehicles under real traffic conditions and evaluate requirements for future regular operation. Cooperative methods based on Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication enabled data exchange between vehicles and infrastructure, improving situational awareness and road safety. Outcomes include improved cooperative traffic management methods, strengthened data interoperability and practical knowledge to support safe deployment of automated fleets in urban environments.

It supports scalable deployment of autonomous shuttles in non-urban regions and contributes to more inclusive, sustainable public transport offerings.

cases.source_description: Understanding why and when neural network models learn effectively remains a fundamental scientific challenge with implications for both artificial intelligence and neuroscience. This project seeks to develop advanced mathematical tools to analyse learning processes in Bayesian Neural Networks as statistical models and to explore parallels with biological neural systems. The research builds on a novel interpretation of local parameter updates in Bayesian Neural Networks as a derivative-free optimisation method, challenging the assumption that such approaches are inherently slow. Using nonparametric and high-dimensional statistical theory, the project investigates the convergence properties and generalisation performance of these models. By establishing rigorous mathematical guarantees, it aims to clarify the statistical mechanisms underlying efficient learning. Insights gained could inform the design of more data-efficient training methods and contribute to the development of neuromorphic computing architectures inspired by biological networks. The project has the potential to open new directions in mathematical statistics while strengthening the conceptual bridge between computational models and brain function.

cases.source_description: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) infections in early life are associated with increased risk of chronic respiratory conditions, including asthma, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. The CLARITY project aims to identify genetic risk factors and molecular pathways linking RSV infection to long-term lung disease. Using national cohort data from Estonia and Spain, the project integrates genomic, clinical and epidemiological datasets to examine virus–host interactions. Advanced computational models analyse cellular networks disrupted by RSV, identifying key pathways associated with inflammatory responses and asthma development. Predictive modelling supports stratification of individuals according to genetic susceptibility and disease risk. The project also screens for drug-like compounds capable of reversing virus-induced molecular alterations. By elucidating causal mechanisms and identifying therapeutic targets, CLARITY seeks to inform personalised prevention strategies and improve treatment options. The findings may extend to other non-communicable diseases triggered by viral infections, enhancing translational impact in respiratory medicine.

cases.source_description: Music rights are traditionally difficult for creators to monetise directly, with complex royalty chains and intermediaries that can reduce transparency for both artists and fans. Anotherblock addresses this by enabling artists and rights-holders to sell defined portions of track-level rights to their community, creating a clearer route for participation and investment in streaming royalties while maintaining a legally enforceable relationship between parties. Stakeholders include creators, collectors, platforms handling royalty reporting, and regulators seeking clarity on how tokenised intellectual property rights should be structured and supervised, with the objective of making rights transfers simpler, auditable, and fairer. The service is implemented by issuing music ownership tokens on Ethereum using the ERC-721 standard, where each token carries a unique identifier and encodes an ownership percentage for a specific song, alongside associated artwork and a linked real-world legal contract defining royalty terms and ownership guarantees. Transactions and ownership history are recorded on-chain, while off-chain legal documentation and royalty flows are aligned to token holdings through platform governance and reporting integrations. The approach can reduce friction and costs in rights distribution, improve transparency of ownership, and create new, engagement-driven revenue options for artists; participation in the European Blockchain Sandbox is used to test compliance pathways and surface regulatory needs for legal certainty in tokenised IP structures.

cases.task: Chunk Works – Universal Security Layer for Distributed Data Protection
cases.context: European Commission; European Institution/Agency; R&D general public services.; Netherlands
cases.implementation: The solution breaks data into encrypted fragments using erasure coding, adds redundancy, and distributes these fragments across multiple locations using distributed ledger technology.
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: As organisations increasingly operate across hybrid and decentralised infrastructures, ensuring data security, availability, and resilience has become more complex. Conventional storage systems face risks from cyberattacks, data loss, and emerging threats such as quantum computing. Chunk Works addresses this challenge by providing a universal security layer that combines strong encryption with resilient data storage. Stakeholders include enterprises, public bodies, and service providers handling sensitive data across cloud, on-premise, and edge environments. The objective is to ensure privacy, integrity, and continuous availability of data without compromising performance or deployment flexibility. The solution breaks data into encrypted fragments using erasure coding, adds redundancy, and distributes these fragments across multiple locations using distributed ledger technology. Post-quantum hybrid encryption protects data against future cryptographic threats, while autonomous recovery mechanisms reconstruct data even if parts are lost or unavailable. The impact includes increased resilience to failures and attacks, reduced risk of data loss, and future-proof security. Chunk Works delivers a scalable, infrastructure-agnostic solution that strengthens trust in digital data management and supports secure operations in increasingly decentralised environments.

Regulators and financial institutions require sophisticated tools to understand complex transaction flows and assess risk in blockchain ecosystems. Coinfirm addresses this need by providing advanced analytics and investigation capabilities for digital assets. Coinfirm supports safer adoption of digital assets and contributes to the integrity and stability of the evolving financial ecosystem.

cases.task: Eonpass: stopping counterfeit goods
cases.context: EUIPO; European Institution/Agency; R&D general public services.; European Union
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Counterfeit goods entering the European Union pose risks to consumer safety, brand integrity, and public revenues, while placing significant strain on customs authorities. Eonpass emerged as a proposed solution following a competition organised by the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO), aiming to improve the detection of fraudulent goods at borders. Stakeholders included EUIPO, customs authorities, logistics providers, and private-sector partners such as EY and Jet Air Service. The objective was to create a shared, trusted mechanism for verifying the authenticity of goods across complex international supply chains. The proposed system used distributed ledger technology to record product identifiers, shipment data, and verification events, enabling customs officials to cross-check goods against tamper-resistant records at the point of entry. Open standards were emphasised to allow interoperability between manufacturers, freight operators, and enforcement agencies. While Eonpass was recognised as the strongest conceptual model in the EUIPO competition, public sources indicate that it remained at proof-of-concept level and was not rolled out as an operational customs system. Nonetheless, the project demonstrated how shared digital ledgers could enhance transparency and trust in border processes, informing later policy and technical discussions on anti-counterfeiting measures.

The platform integrates with enterprise systems and supports selective data disclosure. Selected for the EU Blockchain Regulatory Sandbox, the pilot demonstrates compliance-by-design, improved trust across supply chains and reduced reporting friction. It positions DPPs as a scalable tool for transparency, enabling businesses to meet regulatory demands while supporting greener consumer choices and circular value chains.

Although minor inaccuracies may occur, the system significantly expands real-time accessibility across national broadcasting services.

VET systems are governed by networks of social partners, including employers and trade unions, which often rely on fragmented administrative processes and non-standardised data models. This creates inefficiencies, prolonged verification timelines and reliance on intermediaries for credential validation. Standardised data models enhance interoperability among chambers, councils and institutions. By reducing administrative complexity and strengthening trust in digital verification, the initiative supports cross-border labour mobility and improves transparency in skills recognition. The approach enhances privacy by allowing individuals to control credential sharing while ensuring reliable authentication of vocational qualifications.

Current hiring processes often rely on paper certificates, PDFs or self-declared CVs, requiring time-consuming manual verification by employers. The initiative establishes a decentralised system for issuing and validating employment credentials using the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure. By enabling direct, tamper-evident authentication of employment history, the project enhances efficiency in human resources management and supports a more transparent European labour market ecosystem.

cases.context: NHS; Central-Government; R&D health.; United Kingdom
cases.implementation: The objective is to improve transplant decision-making, make better use of donated organs, and increase the number of patients who can benefit from successful transplants. cases.source_description: Organ transplantation depends on rapid and accurate assessment of donor organs, yet decisions about suitability are complex and time-sensitive, and clinicians must often judge quality under conditions of uncertainty. OrQA was developed to support this process by helping specialists assess whether organs are suitable for kidney and liver transplantation through faster and more consistent image-based evaluation. The objective is to improve transplant decision-making, make better use of donated organs, and increase the number of patients who can benefit from successful transplants. The impact includes the potential for quicker and more reliable assessment, better use of scarce donor organs, and improved outcomes for patients awaiting transplant, alongside operational gains in a highly specialised clinical pathway.

cases.source_description: The City of Bologna is addressing complex urban challenges related to sustainable mobility, energy efficiency, and climate change mitigation, which require coordinated planning across multiple policy domains. City planners, utilities, transport authorities, and citizens all need reliable evidence to support long-term infrastructure investments and behavioural change. The objective of the digital twin initiative is to provide an integrated decision-support environment that allows the city to analyse current conditions and simulate future scenarios before implementing policies or investments. The solution is implemented through a digital replica of the city that integrates data from sensors, administrative systems, and qualitative social data. In mobility, the model combines traffic counts, environmental sensors, and citizen feedback to assess the impact of cycling lanes and tram infrastructure. In the energy domain, it simulates building energy performance to evaluate renovation strategies, incentives, and urban plans aimed at achieving net-zero targets. The digital twin enables scenario testing and cross-sector analysis within a shared platform. As a result, Bologna can design more coherent policies, reduce planning risks, and prioritise investments with higher sustainability impact. The initiative improves transparency, supports data-driven governance, and strengthens the city’s capacity to plan resilient and climate-neutral urban development.

cases.source_description: Aligning national legislation with the European Union acquis requires the translation, interpretation, and integration of very large volumes of legal and regulatory material, making accession an administratively demanding and time-intensive process. In Albania, the government presented this use case as a way to accelerate that work by using ChatGPT to translate EU legal measures and assist with incorporating them into Albanian legal structures. The objective is to reduce the manual burden associated with legal translation and alignment, shorten paperwork timelines, and support faster progress towards EU accession. The implementation uses a large language model to process legal text, support translation into Albanian, and assist with the comparison and integration of EU provisions into the domestic legislative framework. At a conceptual level, the tool functions as a language and legal-text processing assistant for officials dealing with approximation of legislation, rather than as an autonomous decision-maker. The expected impact includes faster handling of large legal-text volumes, reduced administrative effort, and improved capacity to manage a complex accession workload. It also illustrates how generative language technology can be used in public administration to support large-scale legal harmonisation and strategic policy objectives.

cases.source_description: Upper-limb prosthesis abandonment rates can reach 44 %, often due to limited functionality, discomfort and insufficient rehabilitation support. BRAINmade seeks to reduce abandonment by improving motor training and user adaptation through an accessible rehabilitation platform. The project develops immersive virtual reality scenarios controlled by electromyographic (EMG) signals generated by residual limb muscles. Customised, low-cost EMG sensors capture muscle activity and translate it into movements within virtual training environments, enabling patients to practise control strategies even with non-anthropomorphic prostheses. A structured four-week motor training programme reinforces neuromuscular coordination and embodiment of the device. The system integrates hardware and software components designed for affordability and scalability in clinical settings. Early results indicate improved motor performance and user engagement. By enhancing functional outcomes and confidence, the platform aims to lower prosthesis rejection rates, improve quality of life for amputees and modernise rehabilitation practices through cost-effective, technology-enabled training.

The KATSIM project aims to develop a diagnostic device that simulates how patients will see after surgery, supporting personalised clinical decisions. The system uses computational holography to recreate realistic visual distortions associated with different cataract conditions and lens options. Advanced optical modelling and image processing algorithms generate holographic projections that replicate patient-specific vision scenarios. Clinicians can visualise and compare expected outcomes before intervention, improving lens selection accuracy. The project brings together expertise in computational holography, ophthalmology and vision science to validate the technology in clinical environments. By enabling more precise preoperative assessment, the device has potential to improve patient satisfaction, reduce revision procedures and optimise surgical planning. The innovation enhances shared decision-making between clinicians and patients and supports more predictable, outcome-oriented cataract treatment.

In breast cancer care, clinicians need reliable tools to predict how patients will respond to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in order to avoid unnecessary treatment and optimise outcomes. The RadioVal project addresses this challenge by bringing together hospitals, clinicians, researchers, and technology developers across eight clinical sites in Europe and beyond, with the objective of validating radiomics-based decision support in routine breast cancer treatment planning. The project implements advanced radiomics pipelines that extract quantitative features from medical imaging data, combined with machine learning models trained to predict treatment response. These tools are evaluated using harmonised imaging datasets and clinical data, and assessed across multiple dimensions, including technical robustness, algorithmic fairness, clinical usability, and acceptance by healthcare professionals, with integration into existing clinical workflows. The project strengthens confidence in data-driven imaging tools, supports more precise treatment decisions, and aims to reduce over-treatment while improving patient outcomes. By providing robust clinical validation and usability evidence, RadioVal contributes to increased trust, scalability, and responsible adoption of advanced imaging analytics in oncology.

cases.source_description: The growing volume of end-of-life photovoltaic modules presents a sustainability challenge, as current recycling processes recover limited materials and fail to support a truly circular solar economy. To meet environmental and economic goals, the photovoltaic sector needs better traceability, higher-quality material recovery, and stronger links between production, reuse, and recycling. The APOLLO project addresses these challenges by involving manufacturers, recyclers, technology providers, and market actors to establish a circular framework for photovoltaic modules. Its objective is to maximise material recovery, enable reuse and remanufacturing, and reduce environmental impact across the full product lifecycle. The solution is implemented through blockchain-based Digital Product Passports that store secure, trustworthy information on materials, composition, hazards, and lifecycle history of photovoltaic modules. These passports support automated access to data needed for recycling and reuse and are linked to an online marketplace for recovered and refurbished components. The approach improves transparency, traceability, and coordination across the value chain, increases the economic viability of recycling, and supports regulatory compliance. APOLLO enables higher-value material recovery, reduces waste, and creates scalable foundations for a circular photovoltaic industry.

cases.problem: Recognising cardiac arrest during emergency calls is a high-stakes operational challenge, because callers may describe symptoms unclearly and dispatchers must make life-critical decisions within seconds.
cases.task: AI predicts cardian arrest in Copenhagen
cases.context: Copenhagen Emergency Medical Services; Local Government; Hospital services.; Denmark
cases.implementation: The implementation uses a real-time speech-analysis solution that listens to the ongoing emergency call, compares patterns in the dialogue with historical call data, and calculates the probability that the incident involves cardiac arrest. At a conceptual level, the system applies predictive pattern recognition to live call audio and feeds alerts to the medical dispatcher handling the case, functioning as decision support rather than a replacement for human judgement.
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Recognising cardiac arrest during emergency calls is a high-stakes operational challenge, because callers may describe symptoms unclearly and dispatchers must make life-critical decisions within seconds. In Copenhagen, Emergency Medical Services introduced a real-time analytical tool to improve recognition of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest during 112 calls and provide dispatchers with earlier warning when a call matches patterns associated with cardiac arrest. The objective is to increase recognition rates, support faster intervention, and improve survival chances by strengthening dispatcher decision-making during the call itself. The implementation uses a real-time speech-analysis solution that listens to the ongoing emergency call, compares patterns in the dialogue with historical call data, and calculates the probability that the incident involves cardiac arrest. At a conceptual level, the system applies predictive pattern recognition to live call audio and feeds alerts to the medical dispatcher handling the case, functioning as decision support rather than a replacement for human judgement. Reported results indicate that the tool identifies around 85 per cent of cardiac arrests, compared with approximately 75 per cent recognised by dispatchers alone, corresponding to roughly 150 additional patients being recognised before the ambulance arrives. The impact includes faster diagnosis, better quality of emergency response, and more effective use of pre-hospital care resources.

cases.problem: Formentera, a small island with limited carrying capacity, needed a mechanism to better distribute visitor flows and reduce overcrowding in highly frequented areas, while engaging both tourists and residents in sustainable behaviour.
cases.task: Balancing tourist capacity via blockchain in Formentera
cases.context: Consell of Formentera; Local Government; General economic, commercial and labour affair; Spain
cases.implementation: This use case addresses that challenge by involving the island council, tourism authorities, local businesses, residents, and visitors, with the objective of promoting more balanced tourism patterns and sustainable use of space. The solution is implemented through a decentralised incentive system based on blockchain and smart contracts, which integrates real-time data from the island’s Tourism Intelligence System via oracles.
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Tourist destinations with fragile ecosystems face increasing pressure to balance economic benefits from tourism with the protection of natural resources and quality of life for residents. Formentera, a small island with limited carrying capacity, needed a mechanism to better distribute visitor flows and reduce overcrowding in highly frequented areas, while engaging both tourists and residents in sustainable behaviour. This use case addresses that challenge by involving the island council, tourism authorities, local businesses, residents, and visitors, with the objective of promoting more balanced tourism patterns and sustainable use of space. The solution is implemented through a decentralised incentive system based on blockchain and smart contracts, which integrates real-time data from the island’s Tourism Intelligence System via oracles. Based on current capacity and congestion levels, incentives are dynamically issued to encourage visits to less crowded areas or specific activities, such as museums, events, or public transport routes, with transactions recorded on the Alastria network. The approach improves transparency, traceability, and trust in capacity management, enables data-driven redistribution of tourist flows, and enhances visitor experience while protecting sensitive areas. It supports sustainable tourism, reduces pressure on overcrowded sites, and provides a scalable governance model for managing destination carrying capacity.

In regions such as Wildpoldsried, where many households already generate renewable electricity, surplus energy is often fed into central grids instead of being exchanged locally. The Pebbles project addresses this challenge by designing a sustainable and economically viable local energy market within a microgrid. Stakeholders include households, small and medium-sized producers, prosumers, local companies, and distribution network operators. The objective is to establish a replicable model for regional electricity markets that strengthens local value creation and energy autonomy. The solution implements a regional digital trading platform that enables peer-to-peer exchange of green electricity within the microgrid. Transactions between participants are securely recorded and settled using distributed ledger mechanisms, ensuring transparency and trust without central intermediaries. Market rules support flexible pricing and real-time balancing of supply and demand. The project demonstrates improved local consumption of renewable energy, increased economic participation of small actors, and reduced grid dependency. Pebbles delivers a scalable blueprint for decentralised energy markets, supporting the transition towards resilient, community-based energy systems.

The PORO initiative was launched to strengthen European digital sovereignty by providing open, high-quality language models trained on European data. Led by startup SiloGen, in collaboration with the University of Turku and HPLT, the project aims to democratise access to advanced language models while ensuring alignment with European values, research openness and linguistic diversity. Open-source checkpoints enable reuse, fine-tuning and transparent evaluation by public and private actors. The initiative delivers strategic benefits by reducing dependency on non-European providers, improving language coverage for public services and research, and enabling innovation across sectors. PORO establishes a scalable foundation for sovereign European language infrastructure.

cases.task: Vël'OK: Cycling for Survcoins
cases.context: Vël'Ok; Community led; Pollution abatement.; Luxembourg
cases.implementation: After registering via a mobile application, users earn tokens automatically when using shared electric bicycles.
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Local authorities seek practical ways to encourage sustainable mobility and reduce carbon emissions while engaging citizens directly in climate action. In southern Luxembourg, nine municipalities operating the Vël’OK bicycle-sharing scheme introduced Survcoin, a digital reward mechanism designed to incentivise cycling. Stakeholders include municipal authorities, the Vël’OK operator CIGL and registered bicycle users. The objective is to promote low-emission transport while experimenting with alternative, community-based incentive models. Survcoin operates as a blockchain-based virtual currency awarded to users based on kilometres cycled between Vël’OK stations. After registering via a mobile application, users earn tokens automatically when using shared electric bicycles. Importantly, no location tracking is used; distance is calculated by extrapolating trips between stations, protecting user privacy. Blockchain infrastructure ensures transparent issuance, traceability and protection against manipulation. Users can redeem Survcoins within participating local circuits. The pilot demonstrates increased engagement with cycling services and raises awareness of sustainable mobility. It shows how distributed ledger technologies can support local climate objectives, foster behavioural change and enable trust-based incentive systems without intrusive data collection.

cases.context: BiDA - Lab, Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (UAM); Academic-Research; R&D general public services.; Spain

cases.source_description: Public affairs documents shape regulation, compliance and democratic oversight, yet their volume and complexity make systematic analysis challenging for both public institutions and private organisations. This research pilot investigates how large language models can support the classification of public affairs texts. Stakeholders include policymakers, regulatory analysts, companies and researchers. The objective is to improve transparency and accessibility by enabling structured analysis of large document collections. A dataset of over 33,000 public affairs documents, comprising more than 22.5 million tokens, was compiled using automated collection techniques. The task involves multi-label classification across up to 30 policy topics, reflecting the real-world complexity of regulatory texts. Several Spanish-language language models were evaluated under different configurations. The results demonstrate that domain-adapted models can achieve strong performance in classifying specialised documents, significantly reducing manual effort. The study highlights the potential of language models to support regulatory monitoring, policy analysis and corporate compliance. It also identifies challenges related to multilingual performance and domain specificity, providing a methodological foundation for future operational deployments in public affairs analysis.

cases.source_description: Norwegian highway tunnels rely on Automatic Incident Detection (AID) systems to alert control centres to dangerous events, yet approximately 90 % of alerts are false positives due to misinterpretation of visual changes such as shadows or lighting variations. Expected impacts include improved operational efficiency at traffic control centres, faster response to real incidents and enhanced tunnel safety through more reliable automated detection.

cases.source_description: Glaciers are critical natural resources and indicators of climate change, yet monitoring their evolution at scale remains complex, resource-intensive, and fragmented. Public authorities and research institutions require accurate, automated tools to track changes in glacial extent and structure in order to assess long-term impacts on water availability and environmental stability. This use case addresses these needs by supporting climate monitoring through systematic analysis of satellite imagery, involving public administrations, researchers, and environmental agencies. The approach significantly reduces manual analysis effort, improves consistency of measurements across regions, and enables large-scale, repeatable monitoring. It provides more reliable evidence for climate policy, supports water resource planning, and strengthens decision-making by delivering timely, data-driven insights into glacial retreat and its environmental consequences.

cases.source_description: Municipal authorities require comprehensive data to improve seismic resilience, safety and energy efficiency of public buildings. In Florence, a pilot within the BUILDCHAIN project applies the Digital Building LogBook platform to a portfolio of school buildings. Existing data from structural surveys, material testing, seismic performance assessments and safety indices are logged within a decentralised knowledge graph supported by blockchain technology to ensure traceability and data integrity. Analytical tools process these datasets to identify priorities for seismic retrofitting and support intervention planning, including classroom management during works. The platform also integrates escape route management and safety monitoring features. For energy optimisation, smart meters, smart plugs and environmental sensors collect operational data to inform efficiency improvements with minimal intrusion. By consolidating structural and operational information, the pilot enhances evidence-based asset management, supports safer learning environments and enables strategic planning for resilience and sustainability in municipal school infrastructure.

cases.context: Universidad de Granada; Consortium; Housing development.; Spain
cases.implementation: The solution develops a Digital Building Logbook that aggregates structural, environmental, and historical data using a distributed ledger to ensure integrity and traceability.

cases.source_description: Cultural heritage buildings face increasing risks from ageing, pollution, and climate-related stress, while maintenance decisions are often reactive and fragmented across institutions. The BUILDCHAIN project addresses the need for proactive, data-driven management of public and heritage buildings. In the “Hospital Real” pilot in Granada, stakeholders include municipalities, heritage managers, engineers, and conservation experts. The objective is to improve long-term preservation through integrated monitoring, predictive maintenance, and transparent documentation. The solution develops a Digital Building Logbook that aggregates structural, environmental, and historical data using a distributed ledger to ensure integrity and traceability. Sensor data on variables such as moisture, pollution, and vibration are combined with predictive degradation models to forecast deterioration processes. Hybrid analytical models and advanced system representations simulate the impact of inspection and maintenance actions. The project enables proactive interventions, reduces long-term maintenance costs, and improves resilience of heritage assets. BUILDCHAIN delivers a scalable framework for managing public buildings, transforming maintenance from reactive repair to predictive, evidence-based stewardship.

cases.source_description: Designing technologically advanced healthcare facilities requires coordinated management of complex construction, cost and performance data. This BUILDCHAIN pilot applies the Digital Building LogBook methodology to a new hospital in Ljubljana, integrating Building Information Modelling (BIM) with decentralised data management. The project standardises priced bills of quantities (PBoQ) and links them to BIM components through a structured Model Breakdown Structure, ensuring traceability across design phases. The BIM model evolves from conceptual to detailed design and construction, synchronised with cost management processes. Structural health monitoring sensors are incorporated to account for sensitivity of medical equipment to minor displacements. Blockchain-based infrastructure supports secure logging of lifecycle data and interoperability between stakeholders. The approach enhances transparency, improves cost control and strengthens structural performance monitoring. The pilot demonstrates how integrated BIM and distributed ledger technologies can support efficient management of complex hospital infrastructure throughout its lifecycle.

cases.task: Estonian National Gazette with KSI-blockchain
cases.context: Centre of Registers and Information Systems (RIK); Central-Government; Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.; Estonia
cases.implementation: The implementation uses blockchain as one security layer within the Gazette’s protection model, integrating hash values of published XML laws and regulations together with hash values of digitally signed versions into a cryptographic chain.

cases.source_description: When a country relies entirely on a digital legal gazette as the sole official publication of laws and regulations, the integrity of that platform becomes critical, because any unauthorised change could undermine legal certainty across the whole system. In Estonia, the electronic National Gazette has been the only official publication point for laws and regulations since 1 June 2010, creating a need for especially strong safeguards against tampering. The objective is to ensure the trustworthiness and verifiability of the legal record by detecting any unauthorised alteration to published content as quickly as possible. The implementation uses blockchain as one security layer within the Gazette’s protection model, integrating hash values of published XML laws and regulations together with hash values of digitally signed versions into a cryptographic chain. At a conceptual level, this enables regular validation of the information published on the portal and immediate notification if unauthorised changes occur. The impact includes stronger confidence in the authenticity of legal information, improved resilience of a critical public register, and a more robust mechanism for ongoing verification in a fully digital legal-publication environment. It also creates value by showing how blockchain can support trust and integrity in government records without being the entire application architecture.

cases.task: EOGuard - KSI-blockchain to protect earth observation data
cases.context: European Space Agency (ESA); European Institution/Agency; Military defence.; European Union
cases.implementation: The solution is implemented using Guardtime’s Keyless Signature Infrastructure (KSI) blockchain, which generates cryptographic proofs of data integrity, sequence, and time across the entire data lifecycle.
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Earth observation data is increasingly critical for environmental monitoring, security, and scientific research, yet its growing volume and complexity expose it to risks such as tampering, corruption, and loss of provenance. Space agencies, data providers, and downstream users require strong guarantees that data has not been altered throughout its lifecycle. The objective of EOGuard is to ensure trust, integrity, and traceability of Earth observation data without disrupting existing mission infrastructures. The solution is implemented using Guardtime’s Keyless Signature Infrastructure (KSI) blockchain, which generates cryptographic proofs of data integrity, sequence, and time across the entire data lifecycle. From data acquisition and processing to distribution and access, integrity proofs are automatically created and verified, independently of data storage formats or satellite missions. The system integrates with existing databases and workflows with minimal overhead, ensuring compatibility and scalability. EOGuard provides continuous assurance against accidental corruption, malicious interference, or security breaches. The impact is increased trust in Earth observation products, reduced risk for critical decision-making, and improved resilience of space data infrastructures. It enables secure reuse of data at scale, supports regulatory and scientific confidence, and delivers long-term value by safeguarding sensitive and mission-critical information.

cases.task: CyberSEAS (Cybersecurity in the Electrical Power and Energy System) - Estonian pilot
cases.context: Elektrilevi (ELV); Central-Government; Fuel and energy; Estonia
cases.implementation: Guardtime’s MIDA technology, based on KSI blockchain infrastructure, was implemented to provide tamper-evident verification and secure key management.

cases.source_description: Electrical power and energy systems rely on operational technology devices whose firmware updates are typically supplied by manufacturers, creating potential vulnerabilities if update sources or repositories are compromised. The Estonian CyberSEAS pilot aimed to safeguard the integrity of device configurations within Elektrilevi, Estonia’s largest distribution system operator, by ensuring that only authorised firmware could be installed. The solution introduced a centralised control mechanism requiring all firmware updates to be cryptographically signed and validated before deployment. Guardtime’s MIDA technology, based on KSI blockchain infrastructure, was implemented to provide tamper-evident verification and secure key management. The central management system automatically rejected unauthorised or unsigned firmware versions, preventing accidental or malicious installation. By embedding cryptographic assurance into update processes, the pilot strengthened configuration control and reduced cyber risk exposure. The initiative demonstrates how distributed ledger-based integrity mechanisms can enhance resilience of critical infrastructure, supporting secure and trustworthy operation of national energy systems.

cases.task: Swarmchestrate EU project - Parking occupancy magnetometer sensor threshold recalibration
cases.context: FUELICS; Private sector; General public services n.e.c.; Greece
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Urban parking management relies on accurate real-time data, yet sensor-based systems are vulnerable to environmental changes that degrade accuracy and require costly manual recalibration. In particular, magnetometer-based parking sensors are affected by natural fluctuations in the Earth’s magnetic field. The Swarmchestrate project addresses this operational challenge by enabling self-organising sensor networks that adapt autonomously. Stakeholders include municipalities, mobility service providers, and urban infrastructure operators. The objective is to maintain reliable parking occupancy detection while reducing maintenance effort and downtime. The solution connects distributed parking sensors into a coordinated network where decentralised orchestration agents analyse collective magnetic flux data. When abnormal behaviour is detected, sensors automatically recalibrate and reconfigure themselves without manual intervention. Secure coordination and data integrity are ensured through decentralised trust mechanisms and privacy-preserving analytics. The project improves data accuracy, reduces operational costs, and increases system resilience. Swarmchestrate demonstrates how self-organising sensor swarms can support scalable, adaptive urban infrastructure management and provide insights into broader environmental phenomena.

Within the Swarmchestrate framework, a demonstrator explores the creation of a digital twin of natural habitats supported by decentralised orchestration mechanisms. Interdependent computational units, organised as self-organising swarms, are coordinated by distributed orchestration agents operating within a dynamic orchestration space.
