The stakeholders include the City of Považská Bystrica, public transport operators, drivers, passengers, municipal planners and residents who rely on local mobility services. The objective is to make route and timetable planning more efficient while maintaining or improving service quality. The implementation uses an AI-powered optimisation tool that automates aspects of public transport planning, including timetable generation and route scheduling. Conceptually, the system can analyse passenger demand, operational constraints, available drivers, route structures and service-frequency requirements to generate more efficient transport plans. By supporting automated scenario analysis and schedule optimisation, it reduces dependence on manual planning and allows the municipality to respond more flexibly to capacity constraints. The reported impact includes significant annual financial savings, improved passenger satisfaction and reduced per capita CO₂ emissions. These results suggest that the tool delivers both operational and environmental value by using resources more efficiently, improving service attractiveness and supporting more sustainable urban mobility.

cases.source_description: Municipalities often rely on recorded accidents alone to understand road-safety problems, yet this reactive approach can miss hidden risks and delay intervention until serious incidents have already occurred. SAFELY was developed to help local authorities move from monitoring past crashes to proactively identifying hazardous conditions before further harm occurs. The platform addresses the need for a more complete understanding of road safety by combining multiple data sources rather than relying only on official accident counts. The stakeholders include municipalities, traffic planners, road-safety teams and local communities, with the objective of prioritising interventions more effectively, allocate resources with greater precision and strengthen evidence-based transport planning. The solution is implemented as a data-driven analytics platform that integrates accident records with traffic patterns, road geometry, environmental data and citizen feedback. At a conceptual level, the system uses clustering techniques such as DBSCAN and ST-DBSCAN, together with geospatial visualisation, to reveal risk hotspots and hidden hazards that are not obvious in raw crash statistics. These insights are presented through actionable hazard maps and planning outputs that fit municipal workflows and align with standards such as CADaS, GDPR and the European Interoperability Framework. The impact has been measurable: in Şanlıurfa, interventions supported by SAFELY were associated with an over 80% reduction in reported accidents and a 90% drop in injuries between 2014–2015 and 2020–2021. More broadly, the platform offers a cost-efficient, scalable and credible model for saving lives through proactive road-safety management.

cases.source_description: In Madrid, last-mile logistics still depends heavily on a conventional, road-based model in which goods move from DHL facilities into the metropolitan centre mainly by truck and van, often through fragmented arrangements involving external operators. This siloed approach contributes to slower deliveries, road congestion and unnecessary environmental impact, especially in dense urban areas where freight and passenger mobility compete for limited space. The Madrid DELPHI use case addresses this problem by integrating passenger and freight transport more strategically and creating a more sustainable logistics model for urban deliveries. The stakeholders include DHL, metro operators, microhub operators, final-mile couriers and city mobility actors, with the objective of improving delivery efficiency while reducing pressure on the road network. The solution is implemented through a multimodal logistics system in which parcels are pre-sorted into roller cages, transferred to dedicated metro depots and moved through the METRO network before reaching microhubs located in selected stations. From there, KOIKI messengers complete the final delivery on foot or by cargo bike, depending on timing requirements and hub location. At a conceptual level, the system combines data-sharing, multimodal coordination and operational planning within a federated mobility framework. The expected impact is quicker deliveries, lower emissions, reduced congestion and better use of urban transport infrastructure. More broadly, the pilot creates a financially and environmentally more sustainable logistics model for Madrid.

The operational problem is that know-how related to processes, safety procedures, system configuration and energy-management practices is often tacit, poorly digitalised or difficult for workers to access at the moment of need. The project therefore aims to improve industrial efficiency by developing modular, AI-based tools and methodologies that support the full lifecycle of procedural knowledge, from elicitation and management to access and exploitation. Its implementation combines symbolic and subsymbolic AI, data technologies, knowledge-management methods and worker-centred digital tools. The solutions are tested in three industrial scenarios: a white-goods production plant, computer numerical control machines and a microgrid testbed, each presenting different procedural-knowledge requirements. The expected impact is improved productivity, fewer operational errors, better knowledge transfer, stronger worker safety and more efficient energy-related practices. With an overall budget of €3.55 million, the project contributes to Industry 5.0 by prioritising human-centric, flexible and accepted tools for industrial workers rather than automation alone.

cases.source_description: Emergency call centres must gather critical information quickly, even when callers do not speak the local language fluently, yet language barriers can delay understanding at the very moment when speed and precision matter most. The Czech PSAP pilot addressed this challenge by testing whether language-support technology could improve emergency communication in multilingual and tourism-related situations. The stakeholders included call takers, PSAP managers and technology providers, with the objective of strengthening communication quality, supporting operators in multilingual calls and assessing whether the tool could become a practical aid in real emergency environments. The pilot focused on around 70 test calls in different languages and examined how well the solution handled transcription and translation under operational conditions. The implementation used Cestel’s NatalíA natural-language-processing solution, which combines simultaneous language detection, translation, transcription and text-to-speech services. At a conceptual level, the tool was tested as a support layer alongside standard emergency-call handling, helping operators understand incoming speech and access written representations of the exchange. The results showed encouraging potential, but also highlighted important limits, including uneven performance across languages, difficulties preserving the chronology of fast conversations and problems detecting questions in Czech, where intonation is especially important. The impact of the pilot was therefore primarily evaluative: it confirmed the promise of multilingual support in PSAP settings while also identifying clear requirements for better linguistic accuracy, stronger conversation handling and on-premise deployment to meet data-security expectations.

The expected value lies in faster, more accessible multilingual communication, but only once robustness improves sufficiently for demanding emergency-call conditions.

However, the pilot still generated useful insight: it confirmed operational interest in transcription, identified the audio-quality barriers that must be addressed and highlighted downstream opportunities for large-language-model applications. cases.source_description: Monitoring water quality across a river system is a complex task, particularly when environmental changes can emerge quickly and official measurement points alone may not provide enough spatial or temporal coverage. AI.CAN addresses this challenge by combining citizen participation with scientific monitoring to improve aquatic-ecology data collection and analysis along the Oder River. The stakeholders include citizen initiatives, NGOs, environmental associations, researchers and public-interest organisations, with the objective of creating a richer and more distributed evidence base for understanding water conditions and ecological risks. The project also aims to show that collaborative, data-driven water monitoring can be transferable to other river systems and bodies of water. The solution is implemented through sensor boxes deployed by non-governmental and citizen actors, whose data are then analysed together with official monitoring information. At a conceptual level, the system combines distributed environmental sensing, citizen-science participation and analytical models to identify patterns in water-quality conditions and improve interpretation of aquatic data. The collaboration with the Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries and re:edu provides a bridge between grassroots monitoring and scientific expertise. The expected impact is broader data coverage, improved environmental awareness and stronger capacity to detect and understand water-quality issues. More broadly, AI.CAN creates value by making aquatic monitoring more participatory, scalable and evidence-based, while strengthening cooperation between citizens and scientific institutions in environmental stewardship.

Its implementation relies on complex algorithms, advanced sensing infrastructure and a central platform able to communicate with competent authorities. Conceptually, Navigard combines real-time data acquisition, automatic risk detection, vehicle monitoring, enforcement support and road-safety intelligence. The expected impact is faster identification of dangerous events, better coordination between infrastructure operators and police, improved road safety and more proactive management of motorway risks. Autostrade per l’Italia also frames Navigard within a broader “intelligent motorway” strategy involving connected roads, smart service areas, drones, infrastructure monitoring and sensor-enabled maintenance.

cases.source_description: GovTech4All Pilot 1 focused on the challenge of securely sharing sensitive public-sector data across borders while preparing digital public services for future cryptographic risks. Public administrations increasingly depend on data spaces that must remain confidential, interoperable, and resilient over time. Led by LANTIK with GRNET and DINUM, the pilot involved public authorities, infrastructure providers, and European institutions, aiming to protect shared data while preserving usability and compliance. The technical solution combined post-quantum cryptographic algorithms with fully homomorphic encryption, enabling data to be processed while remaining encrypted. An open-source framework was developed, deployable via Docker and accessible through APIs, allowing public bodies to integrate advanced encryption into existing systems without architectural disruption. Data exchanged within cross-border services could be analysed securely without exposing underlying information. The pilot was conducted between mid-2023 and mid-2024 under the Digital Europe Programme. Outcomes included improved long-term data security, reduced exposure to emerging cryptographic threats, and a reusable framework adaptable across administrations. The project strengthened trust in European data spaces while supporting scalability, interoperability, and regulatory alignment for future digital public services.

The operational challenge is that transplant logistics are extremely time-sensitive, while road-based transport can be affected by traffic, distance between hospital sites and coordination constraints. In Turin, the project demonstrated a drone connection between two hospital facilities, aiming to create a replicable model for faster and safer transport of organs, blood, medicines and biological samples. The experimental flight on 1 October 2024 covered around 500 metres between the CTO helipad and the Molinette Genetics building, crossing an urban section of the city and part of the Po river. The drone, developed by ABzero, used a dedicated smart capsule able to maintain appropriate transport conditions. Its implementation combines automatic drone navigation, protected biomedical transport, capsule-based monitoring and integrated AI for continuous control of temperature, humidity and material integrity. The expected impact is shorter medical transport times, improved reliability of transplant logistics and stronger capacity to manage urgent biological deliveries across dense urban environments. In Piedmont, the potential beneficiaries include transplant patients, with 496 organ transplants reported in 2024, 449 of them in Turin.

cases.problem: Previously, relevant data were distributed across fragmented databases, paper records and systems that could not communicate effectively. To address this challenge, Roma Capitale developed the Atlante di Roma Capitale, an integrated digital platform described by the municipality as the city’s digital twin.
cases.task: Rome's Digital Twin - Atlante di Roma Capitale
cases.context: City of Rome; Local Government; Community development.; Italy
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Managing Rome’s extensive territory and public assets requires municipal departments to access consistent, accurate and interoperable information. Previously, relevant data were distributed across fragmented databases, paper records and systems that could not communicate effectively. To address this challenge, Roma Capitale developed the Atlante di Roma Capitale, an integrated digital platform described by the municipality as the city’s digital twin. Launched in July 2026 as an expansion of the existing Atlante del Patrimonio, the platform aims to improve knowledge of the urban territory, strengthen public-asset management and progressively integrate data and services from across the municipal administration. The Atlante is based on a new aerial photogrammetric survey covering the entire municipal territory and provides high-definition cartography with a resolution of approximately 5–7.5 centimetres per pixel. The platform integrates three-dimensional mesh models, Building Information Modelling navigation and tools that allow users to perform measurements directly within the digital environment. Data integrity and verifiability are supported through SHA2-256 digital hashes and a precision photogrammetric processing chain. The platform currently incorporates more than 60% of Roma Capitale’s property portfolio, which can be consulted by category, address, condition and surface area. It also integrates the Atlante del Patrimonio, the three-dimensional Schools Atlas and the Underground Utilities Atlas, although access to the latter is restricted for security reasons. Its open architecture is designed to progressively accommodate additional datasets, services and information from all municipal departments. Roma Capitale intends to complete the digitalisation of its entire property portfolio by 2027. Expected benefits include more coordinated planning and maintenance activities, improved access to municipal information, more efficient management of public assets and greater administrative transparency.

cases.source_description: Protecting world heritage sites requires continuous monitoring while avoiding invasive interventions that could compromise historical integrity. At the Colosseum in Rome, heritage authorities and conservation experts needed a reliable method to detect structural changes and environmental stress without physical alteration of the monument. The objective of this pilot is to support proactive preservation through non-invasive, real-time monitoring. The implementation deploys discreet LoRaWAN®-enabled sensors that collect structural and environmental data and transmit it continuously to a central network server. cases.source_description: Urban EVOLUTION addresses a pressing urban-management challenge: how to reduce air pollution and urban heat-island effects in dense city environments while planning interventions that are practical, evidence-based and replicable. Piloted over 12 months in Naples, Catania and Perugia, the initiative brings together municipalities, research partners and technical specialists to test how Nature-Based Solutions can respond to different climatic and urban conditions. The operational objective is to help cities understand where green infrastructure can deliver the greatest value in lowering emissions, reducing particulate matter and improving thermal comfort, while supporting longer-term planning aligned with climate targets. The solution is implemented through a combination of geospatial analysis, remote sensing and analytical models developed with technological partner Latitudo 40 and supported by WiseTown, TeamDev’s R&D division, and the Universities of Perugia and Palermo. At a conceptual level, Earth-observation data and urban-environment indicators are processed to assess pollution levels, map spatial patterns and estimate the impact of green spaces on CO₂ reduction, particulate capture and temperature mitigation. These outputs provide a decision-support layer for Nature-Based Solution planning across diverse city contexts. The expected impact is improved urban-planning precision, stronger evidence for climate adaptation measures and a scalable model for greener cities. More broadly, the project supports Paris Agreement goals, with the broader ambition of cutting emissions by 50% by 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality by 2050, while showing that urban green spaces could offset up to 40% of city emissions and materially improve air quality.

cases.source_description: Baden-Württemberg launched MEDI:CUS in 2022 to tackle a structural weakness in Germany’s decentralised healthcare IT environment: fragmented systems, limited interoperability and inefficient data exchange across institutions and care sectors. This fragmentation makes it harder for hospitals and other healthcare actors to share information securely, scale digital services and innovate consistently across the system. Backed by five state ministries and a broad coalition that includes all university hospitals and the Baden-Württemberg Hospital Association, the initiative aims to establish by 2026 a connected digital foundation that supports more efficient, trusted and interoperable healthcare operations. The solution is being implemented through MEDI:core, a multi-cloud platform architecture designed to function like an app-store model for healthcare. At a conceptual level, the platform combines Infrastructure-as-a-Service and Software-as-a-Service components delivered through standardised interfaces and protocols, enabling interoperability at technical, semantic, organisational and legal levels. The architecture supports secure health-data exchange, cloud-based services and modular digital applications that can be adopted across institutions without each organisation building separate infrastructure from scratch. Early pilot testing has already demonstrated secure hospital connectivity and the deployment of initial services such as cloud storage and Nextcloud. The expected impact is a more scalable and reliable digital-health ecosystem, lower duplication of effort and faster service rollout across participating institutions. By the end of 2026, the project aims to connect 15 to 20 hospitals, provide usable digital solutions and establish a self-sustaining target organisation, creating both a reference model for health-system transformation and a broader blueprint for trusted public-sector platforms.

cases.source_description: Major urban-regeneration schemes often struggle to involve residents in a way that is timely, understandable and genuinely influential, which can weaken transparency, reduce public acceptance and leave planners without a clear view of community priorities. In Malmö’s Nyhamnen harbour redevelopment, the city sought to address this participation gap by creating a more open and engaging planning process in which citizens could explore proposals and contribute meaningfully to decisions shaping the area’s future. The stakeholders include municipal planners, local residents and other community actors, with the objective of improving dialogue, increasing transparency and ensuring that redevelopment choices are better aligned with public needs and expectations. The solution is implemented through PublicTwin, a digital twin platform that visualises proposed developments and enables interactive exploration of planning data. At a conceptual level, the system combines 3D urban representation, accessible user interfaces and feedback tools that allow residents to review proposed interventions, understand spatial implications and submit suggestions in real time. Public input can then be integrated into planning workflows as part of a more continuous and structured engagement process. The pilot’s impact has been qualitative but significant: it improved transparency, increased citizen participation and strengthened communication between planners and residents. More broadly, the initiative fostered greater trust, supported more inclusive decision-making and demonstrated the business and governance value of digital twins as scalable tools for participatory urban planning and more responsive city development.

cases.source_description: Keeping shared bicycles available where and when users need them is a persistent operational challenge for cities, particularly when demand fluctuates sharply by area and time of day. In Kuopio, the electric bike-sharing scheme regularly faced shortages in high-demand zones and surpluses elsewhere, undermining reliability and limiting its effectiveness as a sustainable mobility option. The pilot was designed to address this imbalance by helping the city and service operators manage fleet distribution more intelligently. The stakeholders include mobility operators, logistics teams, municipal transport planners and users of the bike-sharing system, with the objective of improving service reliability, increasing user satisfaction and encouraging wider uptake of cycling as part of the urban transport mix. The solution is implemented through analysis of historical usage data to identify recurring demand patterns by location and time, followed by predictive forecasting of likely shortages. At a conceptual level, these forecasts feed into an operational system that sends real-time redistribution instructions to logistics operators via SMS or digital channels, guiding targeted rebalancing actions. A feedback loop records completed interventions and reported outcomes, allowing the predictive models to be refined continuously. The pilot resulted in more consistent bike availability, fewer service disruptions and better operational efficiency. More broadly, it improved the user experience, strengthened the attractiveness of sustainable transport and demonstrated a scalable, data-driven approach to managing shared mobility assets more effectively across a city.

The University of Nicosia (UNIC) addressed this by redesigning how a course is delivered, accessed, and certified. The initiative involves the university, students worldwide, academic staff, and external experts from the digital economy, with the objective of experimenting with new models of online learning, certification, and learner engagement. The course “Introduction to NFTs and the Metaverse” is delivered entirely through decentralised digital environments, removing reliance on traditional learning management systems. Registration is enabled through the minting of a free course token, which grants access to learning materials and activities hosted in virtual spaces. Course participation, progress, and completion are recorded through blockchain-based mechanisms, and learners can optionally obtain a completion certificate issued as a non-fungible token on Ethereum. The impact has been significant, with more than 14,000 registrants, demonstrating global reach and strong engagement. The model enhances transparency, verifiability, and learner ownership of credentials, while reducing administrative overhead. It provides UNIC with a scalable, future-oriented education model and offers learners a portable, tamper-proof record of achievement aligned with emerging digital economies.

The stakeholders included municipalities, public-transport planners, technology suppliers and potential passengers, with the objective of exploring how self-driving shuttle services could improve first- and last-mile connectivity while fitting within real urban operating conditions. More broadly, FABULOS created value by reducing uncertainty around automated mobility and supporting cities in planning more connected and innovative transport systems.

Expected impacts include improved understanding of risks and benefits, clearer guidelines for responsible experimentation and stronger institutional capacity to innovate. Qualitative outcomes include enhanced transparency, better alignment between technology and administrative law, and a reusable framework for safely testing digital solutions in the public sector.

cases.source_description: UCRONIA was developed by AMA S.p.A. to address a longstanding operational challenge in Rome’s urban hygiene services: the difficulty of managing a vast, complex and constantly changing city through fragmented information and reactive intervention models. In a metropolitan context where waste collection, street cleaning, environmental conditions, citizen reports and public events all affect service delivery, AMA needed a system capable of improving coordination, anticipating issues earlier and supporting more consistent decision-making. The stakeholders include operational managers, field teams, municipal authorities, citizens and technology partners, with the objective of moving from a reactive to a preventive model of urban hygiene management while improving service quality, sustainability and circular-economy performance. The solution is implemented through a real-time geographic digital twin that maps Rome’s urban infrastructure, including manholes, bins, tree-lined streets, vehicle fleets, citizen reports and environmental data, and feeds this information into a dedicated control room. At a conceptual level, the platform integrates geospatial intelligence, live operational data and decision-support capabilities to optimise routing, asset management and intervention planning across the city. Operated 24/7 in collaboration with partners such as Present S.p.A. and Esri Italia, the system has already shown its practical value during major events including papal funerals and Jubilee celebrations. The impact includes more efficient operations, stronger service continuity, better situational awareness and a scalable model for smart, data-driven urban environmental management.

cases.source_description: As part of the EU-funded iMagine project, the EyeOnWater initiative addresses the challenge of ensuring the quality and reliability of citizen-contributed data for environmental monitoring. Through a smartphone application, citizens submit photographs of natural water bodies such as rivers, lakes, and seas to support large-scale observation of water colour and related ecological indicators. Key stakeholders include citizens, environmental scientists, and research institutions that rely on consistent, high-quality visual data. The objective of the use case is to validate incoming images efficiently and at scale so that only suitable, scientifically usable photographs are incorporated into long-term environmental datasets. The service uses computer vision techniques to automatically assess the suitability of submitted images before they enter scientific workflows. Image segmentation and object detection models, including YOLOv8, are applied to identify whether an image contains a water body and to detect obstructions or irrelevant content. The models are trained on a labeled dataset of more than 10,000 images categorized into different quality classes. The validation pipeline is integrated into the mobile application backend, enabling near real-time processing and automated decision-making on image acceptance or rejection. The automated validation process significantly improves the consistency and reliability of citizen science data while reducing the need for manual review. Real-time filtering ensures that only high-quality images are added to long-term water colour datasets, increasing their scientific value and usability. The approach enhances scalability by allowing large volumes of submissions to be processed efficiently, supports faster data availability for researchers, and improves the user experience by providing immediate feedback on submissions. Overall, the solution strengthens the contribution of citizen science to environmental monitoring and ecological research.

cases.source_description: Residents often struggle to navigate council websites or contact centres to find accurate information on local services, leading to high call volumes and repeated enquiries. Barking and Dagenham Council introduced AI Search and Webchat to streamline access to council services, starting with waste collection and expanding to areas such as housing and council tax. Stakeholders include residents, customer service teams, and service departments, with the objective of resolving most routine questions digitally while preserving accessibility. The solution combines an AI-powered search interface and a conversational webchat tool that uses structured service data, including postcode-based logic, to deliver personalised responses. Both interfaces are integrated with council content systems and continuously refined through community feedback and monitoring. Traditional channels, such as phone and face-to-face support, remain available to ensure inclusivity. The impact has been measurable: the AI Search tool now handles around 18,000 sessions per month with a high first-time hit rate, while the chatbot manages approximately 4,450 conversations monthly with a 93% success rate based on user feedback. Together, the tools have significantly reduced general enquiries and call volumes, improved resident satisfaction, and enabled council staff to focus on more complex cases.

Oak National Academy developed Aila to support teachers in lesson planning while maintaining pedagogical quality and alignment with national curricula. Stakeholders include classroom teachers, school leaders, and curriculum designers, with the objective of saving time, reducing stress, and improving teaching consistency. Aila is implemented as a conversational lesson assistant that combines a large language model with retrieval-augmented generation, drawing exclusively on Oak’s quality-assured lesson repository. cases.source_description: Unauthorised use of official government logos on fraudulent or misleading websites poses risks to citizens and undermines trust in public institutions. HM Revenue & Customs, working with Central-Government partners, developed the Logo Detection and Classification Toolkit to automate the identification of such misuse. Stakeholders include enforcement analysts, government departments, and the public, with the objective of detecting and removing infringing websites quickly and accurately. LDK is implemented as an automated pipeline that scans the web via search engines, scrapes suspicious sites, and applies a deep-learning-based computer vision model to detect government logos. The system flags likely infringements for analyst review, integrating seamlessly into existing enforcement workflows. By automating what was previously a manual and time-consuming process, LDK reduces detection time from days to hours. The impact is significant: analysts can now take down 10–20 infringing URLs per month, with accuracy exceeding 97%. This improves public protection, strengthens brand integrity, and delivers substantial efficiency gains for enforcement teams.

This use case, launched in September 2019 by Cineca, MIT and Italian universities including Padua and Milano-Bicocca, addresses that mismatch by rethinking how academic qualifications are issued and recognised. The stakeholders include universities, students, graduates, employers and international education institutions, with the objective of reducing administrative friction, supporting learner mobility and enabling a more modern concept of stackable and digitally usable credentials. The solution is implemented through blockchain-based issuance of academic certificates using the Blockcerts standard. At a conceptual level, universities create secure, portable and verifiable digital credentials that can be shared by graduates and validated independently without relying on repeated manual confirmation from the issuing institution. This architecture supports trusted authenticity while simplifying exchange across institutions and countries. By replacing or complementing conventional diplomas with digital credentials, the system aligns academic certification with new patterns of lifelong learning and international movement. The expected impact includes less bureaucracy, faster verification, greater convenience for graduates and improved interoperability across educational contexts. More broadly, the project creates value by modernising credential management and positioning universities to support a more flexible, digital and globally connected education ecosystem.

cases.source_description: Before MADRE, the SEPA Creditor Identifier register operated through a centralised process that could take days to deliver codes to participating banks, creating delays, manual administration and unnecessary operational overhead. Banque de France launched MADRE in April 2018 to address this inefficiency and modernise a core financial-infrastructure process through a more distributed and automated model. The stakeholders include the central bank, participating banks and financial-sector operators relying on timely and reliable management of SEPA Creditor Identifiers, with the objective of accelerating issuance, reducing paperwork and improving the efficiency and robustness of registry operations. The solution is implemented through a private Ethereum-based blockchain that decentralises the ICS register and embeds process logic in smart contracts. At a conceptual level, the platform replaces a single central database with a distributed ledger architecture in which authorised participants can interact with shared, synchronised records while automated rules govern validation and issuance steps. This significantly reduces reliance on manual intervention and streamlines the overall process flow. As the first blockchain system brought into production by a central bank, MADRE also served as an important proof point for the operational use of distributed-ledger technology in regulated financial infrastructure. The impact includes a reduction in issuance time from days to minutes, lower processing costs, less paperwork and improved operational efficiency, demonstrating clear business value in speed, reliability and administrative simplification.

cases.source_description: Ukraine developed Diia.Engine to address longstanding weaknesses in public-service delivery, including fragmented administrative systems, dependence on paper-based procedures and limited interoperability between existing digital solutions. These structural problems made service development slower, more expensive and harder to scale consistently across institutions. The platform was introduced to provide government bodies with a common foundation for building digital services more quickly and more uniformly. The stakeholders include national agencies, municipalities, service designers and citizens using digital public services, with the objective of reducing development cost, accelerating delivery and improving standardisation across the public sector. The solution is implemented as a national low-code, open-source platform based on reusable modules and shared digital components, including chatbot functions and automated validators. At a conceptual level, institutions build services by assembling standardised blocks rather than developing each system from scratch, which shortens implementation cycles and improves interoperability. Diia.Engine is now used by 23 government agencies and municipalities; more than 40 digital services have been built on the platform, over 80% of them using standard modules, and around 40% of the population has accessed services created this way. Reported estimates indicate possible annual savings of up to USD 50 million if 100 registries are deployed through the platform. More broadly, Diia.Engine creates value through scalability, lower infrastructure use, faster service delivery and a replicable model for public-sector digital transformation.

cases.source_description: The TRACY project was implemented to address the growing need for secure, efficient, and interoperable use of electronic communications metadata in the investigation of serious and organised crime across EU Member States. Law Enforcement Authorities (LEAs) often face fragmentation in accessing and analyzing telecom data, which hinders cross-border cooperation and slows down criminal investigations. TRACY provides an AI-powered data analytics framework tailored for LEAs, improving the timeliness, accuracy, and interoperability of investigations. Preliminary results indicate a significant improvement in processing time and data correlation across jurisdictions. Pilot implementation of TRACY for 6 months in real cases demonstrated a 1000x acceleration in crime resolution. With the use of visual analytics TRACY manages to pinpoint the perpetrators in all cases outperforming manual resolution. TRACY received positive feedback from over 80% of end-users who rated the tools as user-friendly and operationally relevant. Qualitative feedback also highlighted increased confidence in the legal and ethical compliance of the TRACY system, thanks to its embedded privacy-by-design and auditability features. The solution has achieved its core objectives of (1) demonstrating the feasibility of harmonized metadata analysis workflows, (2) equipping LEAs with scalable analytics tools, and (3) informing EU-wide training and standardisation efforts. By addressing both technological and procedural gaps, TRACY contributes to a more resilient, interoperable, and intelligence-led law enforcement ecosystem in Europe.

For example, the idea of OOTS is to use data that is collected by a certain authority, so that there is no need to copy the data for other authorities. Those can request the information they need from the authority that owns the data. But one needs to know the contents of the data in order to request it in semantically correct manner.

cases.source_description: INPS provides services where users are required to submit various types of documents to support their requests, which must undergo a thorough review to verify their validity. This process involves the manual review of millions of documents annually by operators, all within a constrained timeframe. This involves a wide variety of documents (invoices, contracts, travel tickets, payment receipts, etc), making the process highly time-consuming and error prone. The goal of the project was to streamline and enhance the verification process through AI-powered automation, reducing manual workload, ensuring consistency in checks, and improving response times for citizens. To address these challenges, an innovative solution has been developed, integrating on-premise Generative Artificial Intelligence technologies designed to support operators in document analysis activities. Key features of the solution include: • Automatic classification of documents based on both type and content; • Data extraction and verification, with automated comparison between the information in the documents, the tender requirements, and the associated metadata; • Smart visualization of AI-extracted fields, with automatic highlighting directly within the document for easy reference; • Decision support, offering a detailed summary of the extracted data, flagging any discrepancies, and assisting with manual validation. This solution significantly streamlines the verification process, reducing manual effort and increasing both the speed and consistency of checks, delivering concrete benefits to both staff and citizens. Moreover, the system’s ability to adapt and learn from new data ensures continuous performance improvement, supporting progressively more effective procedure management. The solution aims to deliver benefits for both operators and citizens. Overall, the implementation of Generative AI has proven to be a transformative step in modernizing the document verification process, setting a strong foundation for future innovation and scalability. The next objective is primarily to adopt this solution for the other services within the INPS system.

cases.problem: To address the challenges of bureaucratic language, INPS has launched a structured simplification program aimed at making content understandable to users with a middle school level of education. cases.task: Text Simplification for Citizens with GenAI
cases.context: Italian National Institute of Social Security (INPS); Central-Government; Social protection n.e.c.; Italy
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Clear and accessible communication is essential to ensure that citizens can effectively navigate public services. INPS—Italy’s National Institute of Social Security and the largest welfare institution in Europe—serves approximately 45 million citizens through nearly 500 digital services related to pensions and welfare. The clarity of these service descriptions plays a critical role in guaranteeing equitable access and a positive user experience. To address the challenges of bureaucratic language, INPS has launched a structured simplification program aimed at making content understandable to users with a middle school level of education. Over 700 texts have been manually simplified so far, resulting in an increase in the average Gulpease readability score from 57 to 64—a substantial improvement in accessibility. However, this manual process is labor-intensive, requiring specialised linguistic and legal expertise, and is not easily scalable. The need for plain language in public administration has long been acknowledged in Italy. A 2002 directive still in force emphasizes that “all texts produced by administrations must be designed and written to be understood by those who receive them.” Yet institutional communication remains overly formal and complex, hindering citizens’ ability to fully access and understand critical services. While simplification improves transparency and public trust, it must also preserve the legal precision required for official documentation. To overcome these limitations, INPS has integrated Large Language Models (LLMs) into its simplification workflow, developing a semi-automated system—operating in a human-in-the-loop model—that is both scalable and efficient. This solution can process high volumes of content while ensuring readability, semantic accuracy, and legal compliance. A dedicated evaluation framework was introduced to measure key aspects of the output, including readability, fluency, and content preservation. User testing further validated the approach, confirming the quality of AI-generated content in comparison to both the original and manually simplified texts. The AI-based system delivers expert-level results in a fraction of the time and cost required by manual processes. It enhances INPS’s operational efficiency, standardizes quality across service pages, and ensures that content remains accessible and legally sound. Human oversight guarantees accuracy and relevance, while integrated metrics provide transparency and guide ongoing optimization. A large-scale user study involving A/B testing with 1,620 participants confirmed the model’s effectiveness. AI-generated texts were preferred in over 70% of cases when compared to the original versions and outperformed them across all measured dimensions: fluency (+14.1%), readability (+13.5%), clarity (+11.1%), and engagement (+12.3%). The AI semplified versions outperformed also the corresponding human simplified texts across all the qualitative metrics. Citizens are the ultimate beneficiaries of this transformation. By simplifying complex institutional language, INPS reduces barriers to access for individuals with limited language skills, lower educational attainment, or reading difficulties. More inclusive communication strengthens transparency, encourages greater civic engagement, and builds trust between citizens and institutions. Beyond INPS, this AI-driven approach has strong potential for adoption in other sectors where complex language limits accessibility—such as healthcare, legal services, taxation, and social welfare. Its ability to adapt to diverse regulatory and linguistic contexts makes it a powerful tool for modernising public communication across government systems. In summary, the integration of LLMs into INPS’s content simplification strategy demonstrates how generative AI can enhance accessibility, efficiency, and trust in public services—delivering clear, comprehensible, and citizen-centered communication at scale.

cases.source_description: The Generalitat de Catalunya has piloted a Generative AI–based system for drafting environmental technical reports, developed by the Centre of Telecommunications and Information Technology (CTTI) and the Department of Territory, Housing and Ecologic Transition. The solution addresses the high volume and repetitive nature of authorisations for activities in protected areas—such as mountain races, drone flights, and forest management—where more than 4,500 reports are prepared annually. By combining visual-language models, geospatial algorithms, and a vectorised legal knowledge base, the tool analyses route data and regulations to automatically generate draft reports. The system is fully integrated with the Generalitat’s secure intranet and platforms such as SINATCAT, supports Catalan language outputs, and complies with interoperability, security, and data protection standards. Designed to be modular, scalable, and reusable, it improves efficiency, standardises decision-making, and strengthens public trust by ensuring clearer, more uniform environmental reporting.

By supporting staff rather than replacing their judgement, KIRA improves the administrative knowledge workflow and directly benefits citizens through faster and more dependable handling of requests.

cases.source_description: Pepper at TH Wildau is a deployed library assistant, based on SoftBank’s humanoid platform and the NAOqi software stack. The project adapts Pepper for a 24/7 academic library, where access is card-controlled outside staffed hours. The robot greets visitors, answers common questions, guides users to locations across three floors, gives short tours, and demonstrates equipment such as the printer–scanner–copier. The solution combines scripted behaviors with a lightweight NLP pipeline. Behaviors are authored in Choregraphe/Python as modular, rule-based flows for gestures, tablet prompts, and navigation sequences. Speech interaction uses an open, componentised chain: automatic speech recognition (speech-to-text), intent and entity extraction for library domains (orientation, lending, services, events), response generation from curated templates and FAQs, and text-to-speech. The team prioritises transparent, locally hosted components over closed assistants. For perception and mobility, Pepper uses classical robotics methods for localisation and path planning; autonomous driving is complemented by tablet teleoperation for safety and elevators. Two units are operated: “Wilma” serves in the library as a mobile information point; “Bernd” is used in the RoboticLab for testing and training. Content and dialogs are updated iteratively, with analytics from interactions feeding refinements to intents, utterances, and tour scripts.

cases.source_description: The statutory accident insurer BG ETEM introduced RehaPlus to improve the early identification of complex rehabilitation cases requiring intensive case management. Previously, such cases were often detected late through manual reminders, leading to delayed interventions, higher treatment costs and longer recovery times. RehaPlus applies explainable machine learning models to continuously monitor case data and flag potential high-risk cases weeks earlier than before. This has replaced the outdated manual reminder process with proactive, automated monitoring, while ensuring case officers remain in control of final decisions. The result is improved efficiency, fewer documents to screen or complete, earlier interventions, and better recovery outcomes for insured workers. Since going live in 2021, RehaPlus has delivered high user satisfaction, with more than 90 per cent of staff rating it positively for improving efficiency and quality of work. Built with open-source components such as Python, XGBoost, Scikit-learn, Pandas and Docker, the solution is lightweight, explainable, cost-efficient and fully compliant with GDPR. Its modular architecture makes it portable across infrastructures and scalable to other social accident insurers, with the first reuse planned for 2026. By combining automation with transparency and human oversight, RehaPlus demonstrates how AI can create both internal efficiency gains (G2G) and societal value (G2C) through better rehabilitation outcomes.

cases.task: AI-Based Virtual Assistant for Faster and Reliable Businesses Support
cases.context: Berufsgenossenschaft Energie Textil Elektro Medienerzeugnisse (BG ETEM); Central-Government; Sickness and disability.; Germany
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: The statutory accident insurer BG ETEM developed a virtual assistant (MeinAssistent) to support its “Members and Fees” department, which has seen a sharp increase in inquiries from businesses. Around 70 per cent of queries concern recurring issues such as registration or insurance fees, which were previously handled manually, causing long response times and high workloads. The assistant provides a three-tiered service: immediate answers from a legally verified FAQ catalogue, context-specific responses generated from official ETEM documents with clear source references, and transparent escalation to staff if no automated answer is possible. This ensures businesses receive reliable, accurate, and timely support while keeping human oversight for complex cases. Early results from the pilot show clear benefits: 24/7 accessibility for businesses, faster responses, reduced interruptions for staff, and high trust thanks to transparent answer paths. Pilot users have praised the clarity, reliability, and seamless handover to human officers. Built with open-source components including Python, LangChain, Hugging Face models, FastAPI, and Docker, the system is modular, containerised, and API-based, making it cost-efficient, portable, and adaptable to other contexts. Although still in pilot, the solution is being integrated into the MeineETEM portal and is designed for transfer to other public sector organisations by connecting it to their own FAQs and documents. By combining automation, explainability, and scalability, MeinAssistent strengthens efficiency and accessibility in public service delivery while reducing manual workload for staff.

The system enables citizens to declare the fire-prevention cleaning activities they have undertaken on their plots each season and allows them to report hazardous plots to supervisory authorities, supporting proactive intervention. Its interoperable and user-friendly design ensures accessibility, traceability, and transparency, while statistical analysis capabilities inform policy decisions on fire prevention and civil protection. Akatharista.gov.gr exemplifies a digital governance solution that enhances public participation, strengthens accountability, and safeguards human life, property, and ecosystems.

cases.source_description: The Regional Digital Twin for Climate Change provides a data-driven platform for climate risk assessment, simulation, and decision support, addressing gaps in integrating EU-scale climate data into local and sector-specific operations. It enhances resilience across public services and critical sectors—energy, finance, agriculture, and emergency planning—by combining diverse datasets, AI and physical simulations, and a climate services marketplace. The platform also federates stakeholders, fostering collaboration and trust. Pilot users in Luxembourg report improved risk understanding, faster and more informed decisions, and strengthened public and financial resilience. Technologically, it integrates satellite, in-situ, topographic, and regional data via AI and HPC-powered cloud solutions, offering real-time insights and multi-sectoral services. Designed according to the European Interoperability Framework (EIF), the platform ensures legal, organisational, semantic, and technical interoperability. Transparency is enhanced through dashboards, open data where possible, and workshops for stakeholders. Its modular architecture allows scalable deployment across sectors, regions, and administrative levels, with the potential for broader adoption by other administrations. The project follows a user-centred innovation process, beginning with a Proof of Concept by Thales Alenia Space, LIST, and PwC, incorporating feedback from ministries and critical infrastructure operators to ensure practical, actionable outcomes.

cases.context: Dirección General de Transformación Digital de la Administración de Justicia; Central-Government; General public services n.e.c.; Spain
cases.implementation: The AI infrastructure combines natural language processing, supervised neural networks, Transformer-based models, and GPU-enabled servers, deployed within a secure microservices architecture.

cases.source_description: The Ministry of the Presidency, Justice, and Relations with the Courts has harnessed Artificial Intelligence to manage vast volumes of unstructured legal information and streamline tens of thousands of procedures each year. AI tools support civil servants, judges, magistrates, and prosecutors by extracting and linking relevant information, generating timelines, summarising documents, and assisting with rule-based processes. A key initiative is the automatic transcription of hearings and trials, achieving an estimated 60% time saving, with over 3.28 million transcriptions completed to date, saving more than one million hours of work. AI services also produce plain-language and easy-to-read documents, enhancing accessibility for citizens, including those with functional or intellectual difficulties. The AI infrastructure combines natural language processing, supervised neural networks, Transformer-based models, and GPU-enabled servers, deployed within a secure microservices architecture. Services are accessible via portals such as ADIA and Carpeta Justicia and include anonymisation, document summarisation, intelligent assistants, and translation tools. These tools are integrated across multiple internal applications and are already being reused by other administrations, demonstrating scalability and interoperability. Development followed a user-centred, iterative process involving legal experts, linguists, programmers, and administrative staff. Solutions were piloted on a small scale and then expanded strategically, supported by knowledge-sharing initiatives such as the Justice Digital Transformation Forum. Overall, AI innovations have transformed operations, improved efficiency, fostered a culture of innovation, enhanced accessibility, and strengthened transparency and public trust in the justice system.

cases.source_description: SEDIPUALB@ is a digital platform created by the Provincial Council of Albacete to enable fully digital administrative management for municipalities. Initially launched to serve local governments within the province, it provides a shared, open, and interoperable system that simplifies administrative processes and eliminates barriers such as licensing costs or dependence on political cycles. Delivered as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution, the platform is built on open technologies and deployed in the cloud, ensuring scalability, flexibility, and cost-efficiency. Albacete became the only province in Spain where all municipalities adopted a unified digital management platform. Since then, SEDIPUALB@ has expanded well beyond its original scope. Today, more than 300 public entities—including municipalities, consortia, and universities across seven autonomous regions—use the system. It supports over a million citizens and thousands of concurrent users daily. Governance is collaborative, with technical, legal, and administrative bodies advising on improvements, while costs are distributed among participants according to usage. This model ensures both sustainability and transparency, turning a local project into a national benchmark for digital public administration.

cases.task: AI for Species Protection - Detection of Illegal Online Wildlife Trade
cases.context: AI Lab at the German Environment Agency (UBA) and Federal Nature Conservation Agency; Central-Government; Protection of biodiversity and landscape.; Germany
cases.implementation: The system combines AI-powered image classification, rule-based text analysis, and tailored web scraping to scan thousands of online listings daily, identifying species even when disguised or misspelled.
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Germany’s Federal Agency for Nature Conservation, together with the AI Lab at the German Environment Agency, developed an AI-driven tool to detect illegal online trading of protected species, one of the fastest-growing environmental crimes worldwide. The system combines AI-powered image classification, rule-based text analysis, and tailored web scraping to scan thousands of online listings daily, identifying species even when disguised or misspelled. During a six-month pilot, the tool flagged over 50,000 protected animals from more than 1,250 CITES-listed species, transforming an unmanageable manual task into a scalable, data-driven process. It frees public servants from repetitive screening, allowing them to focus on high-risk cases, improving efficiency, and strengthening enforcement. Built entirely in-house with open-source technologies, the system ensures digital sovereignty, sustainability, and compliance with European interoperability standards. It has already inspired international interest, including from the Czech CITES authority, and provides a transferable model for EU-wide biodiversity protection.

cases.task: Impulsa Autónomo: Intelligent Platform to Personalise Grants and Subsidies for the Self-Employed in Galicia through AI
cases.context: Xunta de Galicia; Regional Government; General economic, commercial and labour affair; Spain
cases.implementation: Its implementation uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation–based generative AI, connected to official databases, to provide personalised recommendations rather than static lists of subsidies.
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Impulsa Autónomo was developed by the Xunta de Galicia to simplify how self-employed professionals identify and access grants, subsidies and support measures. The administrative problem is that funding opportunities are often dispersed across different portals, calls and institutional sources, making it difficult for autónomos to understand which schemes are relevant to their activity, situation and eligibility profile. The platform consolidates this information into a single intelligent portal and widget, reducing fragmentation and improving the user journey. Its implementation uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation–based generative AI, connected to official databases, to provide personalised recommendations rather than static lists of subsidies. The system combines official information retrieval, conversational guidance, personalised publication of subsidies, automatic alerts, BI dashboards, satisfaction monitoring and two-way feedback channels. Early results indicate reductions in search time of more than 60% and over 100 hours of integrated specialised advisory services. The expected impact is faster access to relevant support, lower administrative costs through automated responses, more transparent communication of available aid, and stronger interaction between the administration and self-employed workers. Its design also supports interoperability and regulatory alignment, making it a potentially replicable model for digital public services. The Xunta’s official Oficina Virtual do Autónomo is currently online and provides information on support and grants for self-employment.

cases.source_description: Launched in 2022 by the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Justice and Consumers (DG JUST), this project delivers an EU-wide platform that enables systematic surveillance of online marketplaces across all EU and EEA languages. By simulating human interaction to overcome obstacles like pop-ups, captchas, and hidden content, it ensures access to data that traditional crawlers cannot reach. The platform records dangerous products taken offline, fostering transparency, cross-border cooperation, and a shared view of enforcement progress. With the integration of large language models, the system significantly improves the precision of product identification, reducing false positives and enabling inspectors to focus on genuine risks. This shift accelerates enforcement cycles, supports Member States in handling the growing influx of imported parcels, and enhances consumer protection across the Single Market. Aligned with European interoperability principles and EU product-safety legislation, the platform connects seamlessly with the Safety Gate Rapid Alert System. It provides authorities with a cost-effective, centralised, and secure service that strengthens regulatory enforcement while generating valuable insights for future EU policy-making.

cases.source_description: The GREEN-LOG Last-Mile Digital Control Tower (DCT), developed as part of the EU co-funded GREEN-LOG project, addresses the growing challenges of urban last-mile logistics driven by e-commerce expansion. The platform provides real-time monitoring of delivery assets, near real-time forecasting of transport demand and traffic conditions, and advanced data-driven analytics to enhance operational coordination among logistics service providers, city authorities, and other stakeholders. Leveraging AI-powered predictive models, dynamic multi-modal routing, and Logistics-as-a-Service (LaaS) Marketplace metrics, the system optimises fleet utilisation, reduces carbon emissions, and minimises urban congestion while improving delivery efficiency and reliability. Demonstrations across European cities, including Athens, Barcelona, and Flemish urban areas, have shown reductions in kilometres driven (-35%), travel time (-26%), and the number of stops (-12%), delivering both environmental and economic benefits. The DCT’s flexible, modular architecture enables deployment across diverse urban contexts, supports cross-modal routing, and integrates policy constraints and incentives set by local authorities. Its design aligns with the European Interoperability Framework, ensuring legal, semantic, organisational, and technical interoperability, GDPR compliance, and secure, transparent data sharing. Stakeholder engagement and continuous co-creation have driven usability and adoption, with user satisfaction reaching 90% in early 2026, demonstrating the platform’s effectiveness in supporting sustainable and efficient urban logistics.

cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: Portugal is making it easier for citizens to live, study, work, or retire in other EU countries through the Once-Only Technical System (OOTS), an EU-wide framework that reduces the administrative burden of cross-border procedures. With OOTS, citizens and businesses only need to submit required documents (“evidences”) once, as these can be securely exchanged between public authorities across Member States, including permits, certificates, diplomas, or licenses. In December 2023, Portugal went live with the OOTS Common Services, which enable interoperability between procedure portals across the EU, covering around 80,000 national competent authorities. The system reuses existing technical components like eID and eDelivery, and is developed as open-source, ensuring scalable, secure, and GDPR-compliant operations. OOTS simplifies life events such as registering a vehicle abroad, studying, or running a business, while improving administrative efficiency, trust in shared data, and transparency. Early studies suggest that SMEs and self-employed workers could save up to 50% of costs and time when completing cross-border procedures. Students applying to study abroad can also save days or weeks in administrative processes. Portugal is now progressing to level 5 on the OOTS Acceleratormeter, aiming for the first live transactions in collaboration with the Directorate-General for Higher Education. Through OOTS, Portugal contributes to a seamless EU digital single market, enabling faster, more transparent, and citizen-centric public services across Europe.

cases.task: (AILUME) - Artificial Intelligence-Based Application for the Early Detection of Forest Fire Outbreaks
cases.context: Agency for Technological Modernization of Galicia (AMTEGA) – Xunta de Galicia; Regional Government; Fire-protection services; Spain
cases.implementation: Using advanced deep learning models, optimised YOLO detectors, and vision-language reasoning, the system identifies smoke, filters false alarms, and provides explainable alerts to operators at the Central Coordination Center for Forest Fire Defense.
cases.outcome: UNKNOWN; 원천의 기대효과와 별도 관측 성과는 구분해야 합니다.
cases.source_description: AILUME is an artificial intelligence system developed to strengthen Galicia’s response to one of its greatest environmental threats: forest fires. The region’s vast forest coverage, rural depopulation, and increasing climate change impacts make early detection essential. AILUME addresses this by continuously analysing video streams from the Xunta de Galicia’s forest surveillance camera network, strategically placed across the territory. Using advanced deep learning models, optimised YOLO detectors, and vision-language reasoning, the system identifies smoke, filters false alarms, and provides explainable alerts to operators at the Central Coordination Center for Forest Fire Defense. The platform combines state-of-the-art AI with robust software architecture: a Django-based modular backend, Apache Kafka for distributed real-time processing, PyAV/OpenCV for video capture, and PostgreSQL for structured data management. It includes a human-in-the-loop feedback system, ensuring that operator validation contributes to continuous learning and higher detection accuracy. Designed for resilience and scalability, the solution can handle dozens of concurrent video streams with sub-second data latency, operating 24/7 under real production conditions. Pilot testing launched in August 2025 has confirmed its effectiveness: 86.1% detection success in real-world cases, precision of 98.2%, recall of 99.9%, and detection lead times averaging 18 minutes earlier than official notification channels. The system has already proven especially valuable in depopulated rural areas where traditional surveillance is limited, outperforming commercial alternatives in both accuracy and speed.

cases.source_description: Accessing and interpreting parliamentary data can be complex, particularly when users need to navigate large volumes of legislative information spread across amendments, draft laws, procedural stages and official reports. For the Chamber of Deputies, this creates an operational challenge in making legislative production easier to explore, analyse and verify, both for institutional users and for those supporting parliamentary work. NORMA was developed to simplify that access by enabling more intuitive consultation of the Legislative Observatory. The stakeholders include parliamentary staff, researchers and institutional users who need reliable information on the lawmaking process, with the objective of improving the accessibility, clarity and analytical usability of legislative data. The solution is implemented as a natural-language virtual assistant developed from the Legislab proposal by the Polytechnic University of Milan and the Einaudi Institute for Economics and Finance. At a conceptual level, the system queries certified parliamentary archives and allows users to retrieve information on amendments, legislative texts and the parliamentary progress of bills through conversational interaction. It can also present outputs in charts and tables, making complex legislative information easier to interpret. Because it relies on official archival sources, results can be verified against certified documentation. The expected impact is faster access to legislative information, improved analytical capability and stronger support for the Chamber’s institutional work, while also creating value for statistical and research activities related to legislative production.

cases.context: Alma Human AI; Academic-Research; Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.; Italy
cases.implementation: The solution is implemented as an assisted drafting system developed by the Alma Human AI inter-university consortium, involving the Universities of Bologna, LUISS, the CNR, and the Universities of Verona and Turin.

cases.source_description: Drafting parliamentary amendments is a technically demanding task because proposals must not only reflect the intended policy change, but also comply precisely with strict formal and syntactic rules. For deputies and parliamentary groups, this can make amendment preparation slow, error-prone and heavily dependent on specialist drafting expertise. MSE was designed to address this operational difficulty by supporting the preparation of formally correct amendments directly within the parliamentary drafting process. The stakeholders include deputies, parliamentary commissions and political groups, with the objective of reducing drafting friction, improving formal accuracy and making legislative work more efficient and accessible. The solution is implemented as an assisted drafting system developed by the Alma Human AI inter-university consortium, involving the Universities of Bologna, LUISS, the CNR, and the Universities of Verona and Turin. At a conceptual level, MSE provides a text-editor interface that works directly on draft bills and automatically converts modifications into correctly structured amendment proposals in real time. It also includes an internal chatbot that retrieves relevant supporting documentation, such as dossiers, hearing transcripts and deposited memoranda, and links these to official sources. A further module under development will suggest more refined technical phrasing through natural-language interaction. Currently used on a trial basis by parliamentary groups, MSE is expected to be officially rolled out by the end of 2025, with benefits in drafting speed, reliability and overall legislative workflow efficiency.

cases.source_description: Citizens often find it difficult to obtain clear, trustworthy and easily searchable information about the work of Members of Parliament, even though much of that information is already published in official records. Parliamentary activity is spread across proposals, speeches, committee work, oversight acts and institutional roles, which can make it hard for non-specialists to understand what representatives are doing or to explore parliamentary action on a specific topic. DEPUCHAT was created to reduce that barrier and improve public access to parliamentary information. The stakeholders include citizens, parliamentary institutions and civic users interested in transparency and democratic participation, with the objective of providing fast, certified and intelligible access to MPs’ official activities while maintaining strict limits around the scope of the information provided. The solution is implemented as an experimental generative chatbot developed from a proposal by Roma Tre University and the University of Florence in response to a call from the Chamber of Deputies. At a conceptual level, it uses official parliamentary data, including roles, legislative proposals, speeches, committee work and oversight acts, to support topic-based, person-based and issue-based queries. The system is explicitly confined to parliamentary activity and excludes personal questions. Still in testing, it will undergo further data integration, stress testing and security checks before public release. The expected impact is improved transparency, easier public understanding of parliamentary work and stronger civic engagement through more direct and reliable access to institutional information.

At a conceptual level, these twins integrate data from operational environments and translate them into virtual representations that can be used for simulation, monitoring and decision support. Depending on the use case, this may involve modelling individual service users, territorial systems or public-service environments so that administrators can analyse conditions, detect changes and assess options more effectively. The expected impact is improved service efficiency, better situational awareness and more informed public decision-making. More broadly, the initiative creates value by supporting inclusive and responsive governance, strengthening the practical use of data in administration and providing a scalable framework for smarter management of both people-centred and place-based public services.

cases.source_description: Bus reliability in dense urban corridors is frequently undermined by vehicles that stop or park illegally in reserved bus lanes or at bus stops, disrupting service regularity and slowing public transport operations. In Barcelona, this creates an operational challenge for Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona, which must keep buses moving efficiently while also understanding how frequently such obstructions occur and where they have the greatest impact. The six-month pilot was therefore launched to improve evidence on bus-lane and bus-stop misuse and to assess whether a larger-scale monitoring approach could support future operational improvements. The stakeholders include TMB, bus operators, city mobility authorities and public transport users, with the objective of enhancing bus circulation, reducing interference with service and gathering robust information for possible future enforcement action. The solution is implemented on four buses running on the H12 and D20 routes through cameras mounted inside the front of the vehicles and supplied by Hayden AI. At a conceptual level, the system uses computer-vision techniques to identify static violations, such as unauthorised stopping or parking in restricted areas, while avoiding the recording of licence plates or people during the trial phase. No fines are issued; instead, the system collects statistical and contextual data for evaluation. The expected impact is improved understanding of obstruction patterns, better-informed decisions on rollout and a scalable model for supporting faster, more reliable bus services across the network.

cases.source_description: As renewable generation, storage technologies and electrified demand become more common, distribution networks need new ways to balance local supply and demand without compromising reliability. The Italian PlatOne pilot, led by Areti in the Rome metropolitan area, addressed this challenge by exploring how a local flexibility market could help manage electricity flows more intelligently. The stakeholders included the distribution-system operator, households, commercial users, technology providers and energy-service actors, with the objective of supporting reliable electricity supply while enabling greater use of distributed energy resources and more active citizen participation in energy management. The solution was implemented through a pilot that connected advanced grid automation and monitoring with flexible assets such as cogenerators, residential renewable systems with storage, smart office energy management and electric-vehicle charging infrastructure. At a conceptual level, the platform coordinated these distributed resources through market-oriented and technical mechanisms that allowed flexibility to be identified, exchanged and used in support of network operations. This created a practical environment in which local balancing services could be tested under real operating conditions. The expected impact was more efficient management of electricity demand and supply, improved integration of renewables and stronger operational visibility for the grid operator. More broadly, the pilot created value by demonstrating a pathway towards smarter, more flexible distribution networks that can accommodate electrification and decentralised generation while keeping citizens and local users actively involved.

Traditional production methods often take weeks and cost hundreds of pounds, which limits how much information can realistically be adapted. The council therefore set out to create a faster and more inclusive way to generate accessible documents. The stakeholders include residents with learning disabilities, council communication teams and wider community users who benefit from clearer information, with the objective of improving understanding, reducing production barriers and extending access across more languages and formats. The solution is implemented as an Easy-Read generation tool developed in collaboration with residents and designed to produce simplified documents using clear language, larger fonts and helpful visuals. At a conceptual level, the system automates document adaptation and supports translation into 75 languages, allowing accessible content to be created rapidly while still reflecting the practical needs identified through co-design. The impact is substantial: production time has fallen from weeks to minutes and costs from hundreds of pounds to pennies per page. More broadly, Simply Readable creates value through major efficiency gains, stronger inclusivity and a scalable model for accessible public information.

Traditional digitisation workflows can be time-consuming and resource-intensive, limiting how quickly objects can be documented, interpreted and reused in exhibitions or educational settings.
